# In-House ERP: Micro-Checklist & Build Tracker

Tracks implementation at item level. `[ ]` = not started/open, `[x]` = completed and verified. Mark `[x]` only once actually verified (build/vet/test + live check where the item calls for it).
**Every ask is an item, with a build status (user rule, 2026-10-18):** whatever the user asks for - a whole stage or a one-line enhancement - is recorded here as its own numbered item before building starts, so nothing is missed. Each item ends with `*Status: ...*` (Not started · Building · Built, not verified · Done · Needs decision · Blocked), kept current as work moves, and a stage opens with a per-phase status table (from Stage 88 on).
**Stage Level Status:** Mark a stage header with ✅ ONLY if 100% of the items within it are `[x]` completed. If a stage contains ANY open `[ ]` item (even if it was added later as an addendum), the stage header must be marked as pending ⏳.

> **Legend for historical notes below**: some items were marked `[x]` early and later found to be missing real implementation — those carry a "re-opened"/"correction" note explaining the gap and the fix. This is expected project history, not something to clean up.

> **User, 2026-10-28: answers to the erp-d3 decisions** (session erp-d3; five agents in the main tree; full suite on fresh `custom_erp_dec_full` green for these items - the one gap, `pos_offline_sales` missing from tenant reset, was closed by erp-cd; both erp-d3 batches shipped in 0.19.0 `efc6403`, ledger §304):
> - **49.5.6a Offline sales are validated before they post.** User: *"There will be a validation of offline sales screen. Once its validated it will deduct. Validation of erp barcode vs scanned. Else won't be posted."* A sale sent with `offline_synced` no longer posts stock / GL at checkout: it waits on an Offline sales validation screen, each line's barcode scanned at the till against the item's ERP barcode; only an all-match sale can be validated (then it posts and deducts), anything else is never posted. **Built:** held in `pos_offline_sales`, decided on POS → Offline Sales (capability `pos.offline_validate`: Admin, Store Supervisor), POSOFF-1361 / 1362; Validate replays the held sale through checkout as the original cashier in the original session. `TestStage4956a*` (7); live check on a scratch server. *Status: Done - released 0.19.0 `efc6403` (user in erp-cd: "Push all and deploy all"), deploy pending.*
> - **49.5.6b Vendor state is mandatory; no PO without it.** User: *"This will be avoided by making vendor state mandatory to save and not allow po if state is absent."* A supplier can't be saved without a state; a PO for a supplier with no state is refused; the PO's interstate flag comes from vendor state vs the receiving location's state, so the free `interstate_override` no longer decides it. **Built:** `Vendor.state` always mandatory (a GSTIN fills it, a contradicting one is refused); PURCHA-4961 on save, submit, import, bulk upload, RFQ award and supply proposal; supply type always derived, the override ignored, the PO screen ticks removed. `TestStage4956b*`. *Status: Done - released 0.19.0 `efc6403` (user in erp-cd: "Push all and deploy all"), deploy pending.*
> - **49.5.6c BOM variance acknowledgement only through its own action** (not answered; standard practice taken): `bom_variance_acknowledged` can't be set or cleared by an ordinary Production Order save; a dedicated acknowledge action needs the manufacturing permission and a reason and writes an audit row. **Built:** a save / import can't set or clear it (MFG-4962); the existing acknowledge action needs ProductionOrder update and a reason (MFG-4963 / 4964) and audits the quantities before and after. `TestStage4956c*`. *Status: Done - released 0.19.0 `efc6403` (user in erp-cd: "Push all and deploy all"), deploy pending.*
> - **49.3.2a Unknown client code is refused.** User: *"Fix it."* An unregistered client id at sign-in (or on any pre-sign-in request) is refused instead of landing on the default client. **Built:** `db.GetTenantSchema` answers `ErrUnknownTenant`; a no-session request naming an unregistered client gets SAAS-0188. `TestStage4932a*` (2). *Status: Done - released 0.19.0 `efc6403` (user in erp-cd: "Push all and deploy all"), deploy pending.*
> - **49.2.1a A store switch counts as activity.** User: *"Yes, take std practice."* Any fresh session (sign-in, store switch) stamps the account's last activity, so the dormant sweep never disables someone who is working. **Built:** a store switch and an own password change stamp `last_sign_in_at`; a support session does not. `TestStage4921aStoreSwitchCountsAsActivity`. *Status: Done - released 0.19.0 `efc6403` (user in erp-cd: "Push all and deploy all"), deploy pending.*
> - **47.11.8a Nothing is booked twice with a courier.** User: *"Yes, take std practice. Nothing should be booked twice."* A booking whose request may have reached the courier keeps its claim; a retry checks with the courier first (or waits for a person to confirm) instead of sending a second booking. **Built:** claim and reference saved before the call; an uncertain booking keeps its claim; a retry asks the courier first (Delhivery, Shiprocket) or is refused with INTEGR-4718 until **Resolve** on OMS → Ship; one AWB per courier / one live AWB per parcel (migration `47_11_8a`). `courier_idempotent_47118a_test.go`, `TestCourierResolveBooking47118a`; live check. > - **47.14.2a Date order: day-first by default, per-client choice.** User: *"Yes"* (to "day-first for every client, or a per-client choice?"), read as both: day-first for every client unless that client picks another order in Settings. **Built:** setting `localization.date_order` (DMY default, MDY, YMD); save, import, bulk purchase and prints follow it, lists keep the month name; e-invoice keeps the government format. `TestStage47142a*` (5). *Status: Done - released 0.19.0 `efc6403` (user in erp-cd: "Push all and deploy all"), deploy pending.*

> - **49.5.6d Offline sales follow-ups** (found building 49.5.6a). [needs decision, recommended answers: (1) at the till, an exact SKU scan of an item with no barcode counts as a scan, or its offline sales can never be validated - yes; (2) expected cash at till close includes held offline sales, as its own line - yes; (3) a validated sale posts on the till's sale date, or the validation date when that period is locked - yes]. Limits: a held bill loses its scans on resume; CSV-uploaded lines count as not scanned. User, 2026-10-29: *"all recommended"* - all three yes. **Built:** (1) the till's exact match (`posExactBarcode`) takes the SKU of an item with no barcode, so it adds without the list and counts as scanned; (2) cash of Pending offline sales is its own line `held_offline` in the X-report and the till close, and in expected cash (`sessionHeldOfflineCash`); (3) a validated sale's GL rows, stock ledger lines and bill take the till's sale time (`dateOfflineSaleTx`, as a backdated JV, 73.D.16), or today when that day is in a Closed period; the audit row says which. ### Phase 26.1 — Production-Like Environment
See `docs/operations/go_live_decisions.md` for the decision worksheet + execution steps for every open item in this Phase and Phase 26.2/26.4/26.11 below.
*Some items in this section are closed and archived — see [docs/archive/micro_checklist_closed_stages.md](archive/micro_checklist_closed_stages.md).*

- [ ] **26.1.3b** Activate the Cloudflare edge WAF — managed rules, L7 DDoS absorption and bot controls. The domain and zone now exist (`wholeops.in`, 2026-08-14), so the external prerequisite is met; both records are still grey-cloud.
  - **⚠️ Correction (2026-08-15): "pure activation" was wrong, and the reason is worth keeping.** The plan of record was orange-cloud + CIDRs in two places + lock the origin. That combination **breaks Let's Encrypt renewal on this box**: once the origin firewall admits only Cloudflare, ACME cannot reach it — TLS-ALPN-01 cannot work through a proxy that terminates TLS, and HTTP-01 through the Cloudflare proxy is documented as unreliable. Nothing would have failed on the day; `app.wholeops.in`'s certificate would simply have stopped renewing and expired on **2026-11-12**, with the per-tenant on-demand path breaking sooner. DNS-01 is the usual escape and is refused here for the reason 26.1.3a already gave: it needs a provider plugin, therefore `xcaddy`, therefore a custom Caddy binary to keep patched.
  - **Resolution (user decision, 2026-08-15): a Cloudflare Origin CA certificate** — free, 15-year, wildcard, issued by Cloudflare and trusted only by Cloudflare, which is exactly the CF↔origin hop. No ACME, no plugin, no renewal, and it is what makes a fully locked-down origin possible rather than merely aspirational.
  - **Repository work for this is DONE (2026-08-15) and was not previously counted:** `deploy/enable_tls.sh` gained a `--cloudflare --origin-cert --origin-key` mode and `deploy/Caddyfile` was parameterised so **one** file describes both postures instead of two files drifting. `--cloudflare` fetches Cloudflare's published CIDRs at install time (never hardcoded — a stale list silently mis-attributes client IPs), **fails closed if the fetch fails** rather than installing a partial trust list, writes them into *both* Caddy's `trusted_proxies` (with `trusted_proxies_strict`) *and* `TRUSTED_PROXY_CIDRS` in `/etc/erp/erp.env`, and restarts the app. One command owns both halves because their drift is silent: an unlisted edge node is mistaken for the client and every visitor collapses into one rate-limit bucket. It also **inverts the DNS pre-flight check** instead of skipping it — in `--cloudflare` mode the name must resolve *into* a Cloudflare range, because installing an Origin CA certificate while the record is still grey-cloud serves browsers a certificate only Cloudflare trusts and takes the site down.
  - **Still open — the parts that are genuinely portal-side:** orange-cloud both records, SSL/TLS mode → Full (strict), generate the Origin CA certificate, enable the free managed WAF ruleset + Bot Fight Mode + Authenticated Origin Pulls, a rate-limiting rule on `/api/v1/login`, a cache-bypass rule (Cloudflare caches `.js`/`.css` by default and `public/app.js` has no content hash in its name, so a deploy would otherwise serve stale JS), and restricting inbound 80/443 in the **DigitalOcean cloud firewall** — not just `ufw`, which was never what was blocking traffic here (44.9).

Licensing fear doesn't apply (QZ is LGPL-2.1); no surveyed alternative adoptable; a rebranded `qzind/tray` build worked but was scrapped at 138.5MB. **Built:** clean-room **Go** agent at `../PrintBridge/` speaking QZ's wire protocol exactly, so `public/qz-print.js` needs **zero changes**; zero dependencies, no LGPL obligation; covers 100% of what the ERP calls. **Deployment = one URL:** double-click `PrintBridge\Make-Installer.cmd`, type the client's ERP address → it produces **both** `printbridge-setup-<host>.exe` (Windows, 2.8MB) and `printbridge-mac-<host>.zip` (macOS, 6.5MB). No certificate files: the agent trusts the browser-reported `Origin` against the configured address (exact scheme+host+port), signatures still verified. **Verified on Windows:** origin-trust attack tests; real Chromium trusts the configured origin and refuses any other with the same page+cert; 10/10 protocol tests over `ws://` and `wss://`; raw ZPL byte-exact to a real queue; PDF via WinRT; HTML via headless Edge; install→upgrade→uninstall clean; logo embedded in exe/installer/tray via a hand-written resource object; the installed agent's log shows the **real ERP client** (cert "Custom ERP Print Authority") completing the handshake, correctly refused from unconfigured dev ports 8168/8169. **macOS (2026-10-18, client has a Mac):** CUPS backend (`lp`/`lpstat`, LANG=C), LaunchAgent start-at-login, keychain trust via `security` for https ERPs, double-click `PrintBridge.app` installs / shows status / uninstalls through native `osascript` dialogs; universal Intel+Apple-Silicon binary and the .app zip are assembled **on Windows** by `agent/cmd/mkmacapp`. Verified without a Mac: darwin/arm64, darwin/amd64 and linux build + vet clean; CUPS-output parsing, LaunchAgent plist, AppleScript escaping and .icns unit-tested; zip re-read confirms the exec bit, a valid universal Mach-O, and the ad-hoc code signature M-series Macs require; minimum macOS read from the binary (13.0). **No menu-bar icon on Mac** (needs AppKit/cgo). **Unsigned:** each Mac needs a one-time System Settings → Privacy & Security → *Open Anyway*; removing it needs Apple notarisation ($99/yr Apple Developer account) [needs decision: user]. **Also fixed:** a second copy started from the Start menu while running (now single-instance); `$PSScriptRoot` empty in a PS 5.1 param default broke `Make-Installer` on double-click; Roaming-dir TLS private key; empty GUI-build log; leaked trust roots; silent-install certificate prompt. **Open:** (1) **first real Mac install** — expect it to surface something; (2) physical print on the attached `Y468BT Label` (same gap as 31.1.8); (3) a real print driven by the running ERP; (4) Linux has no installer; (5) USB/HID/serial/file/status-listener calls unbuilt (ERP uses none). ## Stage 34 — Market intelligence / competitor pricing ⏳ (opened 2026-08-06; 34.1-34.3 built 2026-08-07, 34.4-34.6 still gated)

**Source:** [docs/product/research/market-intelligence.md](product/research/market-intelligence.md), the knowledge kept from the retired OmniCore/"Buying Catalog" Python project (see `project_ledger.md` §81). **Nothing in this Stage is approved work** — it is the buildable shape of the one genuinely net-new concept that project held, written down so the analysis isn't repeated. `engines/marketplace.go` covers courier serviceability, labels/manifests, delivery/RTO and settlement reconciliation; it does **not** do competitor-price or catalog harvesting.

**The constraint that shapes the whole Stage.** `go.mod` carries exactly two dependencies (`lib/pq`, `x/crypto`) and there is no vendor directory, so **there is no HTML parser available**. Anything needing DOM traversal means a new dependency, and a headless browser (the retired project used Playwright) means a new *runtime*, not just a library — both against `CLAUDE.md`'s first principle. That single fact is what splits 34.1-34.3 (buildable now, stdlib only) from 34.4-34.5 (gated).

**Sequencing:** 34.6 is the real gate. Do not start 34.4 before it is answered, and 34.1-34.3 are worth doing regardless of how it lands, because they are how the data gets *used* no matter where it comes from.

### 34.4-34.5 — gated, do not start before 34.6

- [ ] **34.4** JSON-endpoint harvester, **stdlib only**. This is feasible precisely because of the reference doc's headline finding: **Myntra ships its whole search result set as an embedded `window.__myx` JSON blob** (fallback `window.__m_initial_state`), so `net/http` + `regexp` + `encoding/json` are sufficient — **no browser and no HTML parser**. Adopt the retired project's two-phase shape: harvest raw responses to disk under a bounded worker pool, skip any file already present and non-trivial (free resumability *and* cache), then parse offline in a second pass so a parser bug costs no re-fetch and no re-ban. **[needs user decision — gated on 34.6]**
- [ ] **34.5** DOM-based extraction for Amazon/Flipkart/Meesho/eBay. **Recommend NOT building.** **User approved the recommendation 2026-10-18: not built.** It needs an HTML parser dependency at minimum and realistically a headless browser (all four sites are JS-rendered and actively anti-bot), which is a new runtime on a 454MB droplet. It is also the part that rots fastest — the retired project's own final commit was "Fix: Myntra scrapping logic", and its Flipkart parser was already dead code by the time it was abandoned. If competitor coverage beyond a JSON-endpoint source is genuinely needed, a **paid pricing-data API** is the lighter answer than owning scrapers. **[needs design decision: buy vs build vs skip]**

### 34.6 — the gate

- [ ] **34.6** Legal/ToS position on automated collection. Marketplace terms generally prohibit scraping, and this is a **multi-tenant SaaS** — harvesting on tenants' behalf carries a different risk profile than a single merchant scraping for their own buying decisions, which is what the retired project was. Needs an explicit answer on: which sources are acceptable, whether `robots.txt` is to be honoured, request-rate ceilings, and whether harvested competitor data may be retained per-tenant or only shown transiently. **[needs user input — this is a business/legal decision, not an engineering one, and 34.4/34.5 stay blocked until it lands]**

## Stages 35-39 — Parity Master Plan ⏳ (opened 2026-08-09; **release train R1 = 35.1/35.2/35.3 built 2026-08-11**; **35 and 37 closed & archived 2026-09-27** — only Stage 38 (38.2d) and Stage 39 (39.18) remain open, each deliberately deferred)

Consolidated from four external benchmarks the user named — [Unicommerce OMS](https://unicommerce.com/products/multichannel-order-management-system/) + the [Uniware documentation portal](https://documentation.unicommerce.com/), the [Unbxd PIM help centre](https://help.pim.unbxd.com/help-documentation/), [SAP Help](https://help.sap.com/) and [Microsoft Dynamics 365](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics-365/) — each reconciled against real code. **Full per-item detail, sizing, sequencing, the 8 open decisions and the explicit out-of-scope list live in [docs/archive/legacy/parity-master-plan.md](archive/legacy/parity-master-plan.md)**; this section is the tracker skeleton only, the same relationship Stage 26.12 has to `oms_master_blueprint_reference.md`.

**Total ≈118 items, ≈61-79 sessions (~3-4 months at this repo's cadence), organised into 7 release trains (R1-R7).** Honest framing carried over from the plan: Unicommerce and Unbxd parity are achievable; **SAP module-count parity is not a coherent goal and is explicitly not being attempted** — Business Central is the ERP benchmark, SAP is read only as a concept checklist.

**The three structural debts R1 exists to clear** (all are existing deliberate deferrals, not new scope): channel orders still land as `POSCart` rather than `SalesOrder` (26.12.1's explicit carve-out), there is no OMS console at all, and the order→shipment→invoice chain is unwired for `SalesOrder` (26.12.3's explicit carve-out).

> ✅ **RESOLVED 2026-08-13 — the dev databases are UTF-8 and the 20.6 defect is closed.** The problem, for the record: `migrations_stage37_1_currency_foundation.sql` seeds `₹`, the dev cluster was **WIN1252**, and SQLSTATE 22P05 stopped the migration runner dead — so every migration from Stage 37.1 onward (37.1.2, 38.2, 38.3, 35.3.7) was blocked. Fixed by dump-and-restore rather than by mangling the migration: `pg_dump --encoding=UTF8` → `CREATE DATABASE ... ENCODING 'UTF8' LOCALE_PROVIDER icu ICU_LOCALE 'en-US' TEMPLATE template0` → restore → rename. **ICU `en-US`, not `C`**, so linguistic sort order matches the old `English_United States.1252` collation instead of silently switching every `ORDER BY` on text to byte order. Verified lossless before the swap: 127 tables identical exact row counts and a matching `md5` content checksum over `tenant_default.documents`. Both `custom_erp` (62 MB) and `custom_erp_test` (the restore-drill target, which would have hit the identical wall) were converted. All 5 blocked migrations then applied, `₹` stored correctly (1 char / 3 bytes), CJK/Arabic/emoji now storable, and `go test ./... -p 1` is green against the converted database. **The originals are retained as `custom_erp_win1252_backup` and `custom_erp_test_win1252_backup`** — nothing was dropped, so the swap is reversible with two `ALTER DATABASE ... RENAME`. Drop them once you are satisfied. Production was always UTF-8 and was never affected.
> - **Finished at the cluster level 2026-08-13**: `template1` — what a bare `CREATE DATABASE` copies, and therefore what was still minting broken databases after the two application databases were converted — was recreated from `template0` as UTF8 + ICU `en-US`. It was pristine, so no user data was involved, and the clause was proven on a throwaway first so the cluster was never left without a `template1`. A database created with no encoding clause at all now comes out UTF-8. `template0` stays WIN1252 **by design** (it is the one template a differing encoding may be copied from); the `postgres` maintenance DB stays WIN1252 by decision, as it mints nothing and holds only retired-WMS debris.
> - **The conversion also exposed how much the 35.3.7 sweeper had to clean**: `custom_erp` held **5,395 orphaned reservations** — stock held out of the sellable pool against lines that were cancelled or gone — which the sweeper drained to 0 with no negative `reserved` counts. That is the leak 35.3.7 was written for, measured on real accumulated data.
>
> ⚠️ **The three "not applied" migrations below ARE APPLIED TO PRODUCTION as of 2026-08-11 16:47:34Z. The safety boundary they were written against no longer exists.** 36.1, 37.1 and 38.2 each record their migration as deliberately unapplied (`BEGIN`/`ROLLBACK`-tested only). That was true when written, and it stopped being true the moment they were committed: `db/migrate.go` does `//go:embed *.sql`, so every `.sql` file sitting in `db/` is embedded and applied by any `erp-server -migrate` or `deploy.ps1` run, with no further decision and no way to scope it. A deploy attempt on 2026-08-11 applied all three to the live droplet. **The existing §6 guard — `git status --porcelain db/` — cannot catch this**, because it only detects *untracked* `.sql` files and these are tracked. Nothing broke (all three are additive and idempotent; 38.2's keys were unusable at the time because no `/api/public/v1` route was registered — **that is no longer true as of the 2026-08-13 `20a8878` deploy**, which registered the four read-only routes and applied the remaining three migrations, `35_3_7`, `37_1_2` and `38_3_5_9`, so an issued key now reaches a live scoped surface), but the lesson generalises: **"unapplied" is never a durable property of a committed migration, and must not be used as the safety boundary for anything.** Verify with `erp-server -migrate-status` rather than inferring from a stage's own notes.

### Stage 38 — Platform & extensibility — ≈8-10 sessions
*Some items in this section are closed and archived — see [docs/archive/micro_checklist_closed_stages.md](archive/micro_checklist_closed_stages.md).*

- [x] **38.2** API credentials: per-tenant keys/OAuth2 client credentials with scopes, rotation, revocation — **API-key branch built 2026-08-11; OAuth2 client credentials built 2026-10-17 (38.2d)**
  - [x] **38.2a** Tenant-scoped opaque API keys — 256-bit `crypto/rand` secret, operator-visible prefix, one-time plaintext return and SHA-256 digest-only storage. Separate raw security table; neither generic documents nor list responses can expose the digest.
  - [x] **38.2b** Explicit allowlisted scopes, expiry, constant-time secret comparison and one generic authentication failure for malformed/unknown/revoked/expired/mismatched keys.
  - [x] **38.2c** Super Admin issue/list/atomic-rotate/revoke endpoints with existing audit-log events; rotation revokes the old key in the same transaction.
  - [x] **38.2d** OAuth2 client-credentials grant — still open; do not add it unless an integration needs standards-based token exchange rather than the now-built opaque-key path. *Done 2026-10-17 (batch C, plan: "38.2 is OAuth2 client credentials only"; SSO/SCIM D10 out of scope). An OAuth client is an API credential with `auth_mode = oauth_client` (one inventory: scopes, expiry, rotation, revocation, budgets, traffic log - 49.2.7's convergence): client_id = key prefix, client_secret = the key, refused as a direct bearer. `POST /api/public/v1/oauth/token` (client_credentials only - no password grant, no refresh; HTTP Basic or form; RFC 6749 errors; 30/min per address; no-store) issues `erp_at_` tokens: 15 min, never past the client's expiry, digest-only storage (`api_oauth_tokens`), bound to the tenant, scopes a subset of the client's. Rotation keeps the mode and ends the old secret's tokens; revocation ends all tokens; expired digests swept with the API logs. OpenAPI publishes an `OAuth2ClientCredentials` scheme. Admin screen: **Extension Hooks → API access** (list first, + New API access, secret shown once, Rotate, Revoke, Recent calls). Migration `migrations_stage38_2_oauth_client_credentials.sql` (+ provisioning clone list). Tests: `TestOAuthClientCredentialsLifecycle`, `TestAPICredentialLifecycle` (fixture updated), `TestOAuthTokenEndpointAndBearerUse`, OpenAPI/manifest; Chrome: issue client, token 200 (899 s), data call 200, both calls in Recent calls with correlation ids, revoke -> token 401.*

## Stage 47 — Deep persona audit remediation: trustworthy, lightweight, self-operable ERP ⏳ (planned 2026-09-01; ≈30-45 sessions, release-gated)

Source of record: [`audits/ERP_DEEP_PERSONA_AUDIT_2026-09-01.md`](archive/audits/erp-deep-persona-audit-2026-09-01.md) (live HTTP + browser + code + database evidence) and [`audits/LIGHTWEIGHT_SMOOTHNESS_PLAN_2026-09-01.md`](archive/audits/lightweight-smoothness-plan-2026-09-01.md) (first-principles architecture, resource budgets and sequencing). The documentation reorganization needed to keep the resulting product supportable is separately planned in [`audits/DOCUMENTATION_ARCHITECTURE_PLAN_2026-09-01.md`](archive/audits/documentation-architecture-plan-2026-09-01.md).

**Why this Stage exists:** the audit found that breadth is ahead of control integrity. A fast screen is not smooth when a Cashier can read payroll/trial balance/system logs, a tampered POS client can choose price/cost, a failed checkout can leave stock posted and deduct it again on retry, a partial return can be replayed, a 3PL allocation can cross owners, or a phone-sized WMS task cannot accept an alphanumeric Wave ID. Stage 47 is therefore a trust-and-operability program, not another module expansion.

**Release rule:** 47.R0 (47.0-47.7) is the critical path. Do not call payroll/privacy, high-value POS, mixed-owner 3PL, mobile/RF WMS, or regulated audit-trail use Production-ready until its applicable R0 gates pass. Existing Stage 37-39 work may continue in parallel only where it does not change the same authorization, POS/return, inventory-owner, audit, or mobile foundations.

**Lightweight constitution for every 47.x item:** preserve the Go modular monolith + PostgreSQL + vanilla-JS topology. No mandatory Redis/Kafka/Elasticsearch/Kubernetes/frontend framework/Node runtime or new production service unless a measured SLO and an ADR prove PostgreSQL/stdlib cannot meet it. Every item records executable/RSS/browser-byte/database-growth/background-work/retention delta. Budgets: stripped binary ≤25 MiB (audit baseline 16.59), idle small-tenant RSS ≤80 MiB (baseline ≈65), cold core transfer ≤180 KiB compressed (baseline ≈287), core JS before interaction ≤120 KiB gzip (baseline ≈237), no unbounded list/report endpoint, no generic failure at the specified normal-screen burst, audit/security hot data ≤20% of hot DB after the legally reviewed retention design (baseline ≈71%), zero mandatory external runtime downloads (no `npm`/`npx`/CDN/remote-font dependency to build or start), p75 LCP ≤1.5s and p75 INP ≤200ms on the reference journeys, cached view-switch p95 ≤250ms, and server p95 ≤150ms/p99 ≤500ms per endpoint under representative load.

Converted mechanically after classifying every handler first: 107 of 109 were a single function call, and the two that were not became named functions (`goToDefaultView`, `selectFieldText`) because the dispatcher calls one function per action and has no statement sequencing — sequencing would mean evaluating source, which is the thing being removed. **This was a security fix, not only a CSP enabler**: an inline handler interpolated its arguments as JavaScript source inside an HTML attribute, so a record id, SKU or doctype containing a quote closed the attribute and the string and executed whatever followed — a live injection sink wherever that value came from imported data, a connector payload, a report row or a CSV cell. Arguments now travel JSON-encoded and HTML-escaped, so a hostile value can only arrive as data. **The new harness found a latent primitive in the dispatcher itself**: `window['eval']` is a function, so a hostile `data-act` name with a string argument would have been arbitrary code execution. `resolveActionFunction` now requires a plain identifier that is an **own** property of `window` (excluding `constructor`/`__proto__`/`toString`) and is not a native built-in — an allowlist by construction rather than a denylist chasing the platform. Not reachable today (every name is a string literal in this repository), so defence in depth rather than a patched hole. **CSP flipped report-only -> blocking**, both phases measured in real Chromium across all 29 dispatched views: the strict candidate reported **zero** violations of any directive *before* it was enforced (that is what authorised the flip), and after enforcing `script-src 'self'` — zero enforced violations, zero `script-src` violations, zero page errors, re-confirmed a third time after the dispatcher hardening. **No nonce and no hash list, deliberately**: there are no inline `<script>` blocks for a nonce to permit (all six scripts are external files), a nonce would add a per-request value that defeats static caching of `index.html`, and `script-src` nonces do not whitelist handler *attributes* anyway — that needs `'unsafe-hashes'`, a weaker position than removing them. The report-only header now carries the next candidate, strict `style-src`, whose 629 inline-style violations are visible but not enforced, so the same two-phase mechanism is in place for that step. All **128** `data-act` reference sites were also checked statically against every way this codebase publishes a function to `window`; all resolve except four pre-existing dangling names in dead `index.html` modal markup (reported, not fixed — removing those overlays is a UI decision). `TestSecurityHeadersEnforcesStrictScriptSrc` now guards the inverse of what it used to: that the exception is not quietly reintroduced. - [ ] **47.11 Graceful request control, worker ownership and side-effect safety** — closes A-10/A-11/A-15/A-16/A-17/A-44; extends rather than duplicates Stage 38.6.
  - [x] **47.11.1** Bound/prune rate-limit and tenant-concurrency state; define replica-consistent semantics using PostgreSQL only where shared state is required. Unique invalid keys cannot grow memory indefinitely.
    — *Done 2026-10-11.* **Measured first** (200,000 requests each, old code): rotating IPs left
    200,000 limiter keys (+22.2 MB), and rotating junk bearer tokens from one IP left 200,000
    keys (+23.8 MB). None were ever freed, and the junk-token run was **never refused**: each junk
    token got its own fresh budget, a full per-IP limit bypass. The tenant in-flight map kept
    every tenant id it had seen at 0, and before auth that id can come from `X-Tenant-ID` or
    `?tenant_id=`. **Fix, `internal/server/middleware.go` only:**
    - `sessionFingerprint` gives a per-session bucket only to a token that passes
      `engines.ParseToken` (signature + expiry, in-memory keyring, no DB), so junk shares the
      address's budget.
    - `RateLimiter` sweeps keys idle past the window (at most every 10 s) and caps its table at
      100,000 keys (~11 MB). A new key that finds it full, after a forced sweep at most once a
      second, counts in a shared overflow bucket per limit. Known callers keep their own budget,
      and overflow is logged once per sweep.
    - `tenantConcurrencyLimiter.release` deletes a tenant at 0.

    **Replica semantics** (written in the code and ADMIN_GUIDE §D): both are per process by
    design. Behind N replicas a caller can draw up to N× a budget, and the tenant cap protects
    each process's own pool. State that must be shared is already in PostgreSQL (account lockout
    `users.failed_login_count`/`locked_until`, MFA/reset tokens, `credential_version`), so no new
    shared table was needed. **Tests** (`internal/server/rate_limit_bounds_test.go`): 300,000
    rotating keys → 100,001 keys / +11.1 MB; sweep after the window; a full table keeps an
    existing 5/min budget exact; 5,000 junk tenants leave an empty map with the cap intact;
    through `apiMiddleware`, junk tokens hit the address's budget on request 101 and two signed
    sessions behind one address keep separate budgets (Stage 30.5.9). The junk-token and tenant
    tests are A/B-confirmed to fail on HEAD.

## Stage 48 — Documentation architecture, governance, controlled migration and deletion ⏳ (in progress; started 2026-09-06, reviewed/rebuilt 2026-09-10)

Source of record: [`audits/DOCUMENTATION_ARCHITECTURE_PLAN_2026-09-01.md`](archive/audits/documentation-architecture-plan-2026-09-01.md). Evidence inputs: the [deep persona audit](archive/audits/erp-deep-persona-audit-2026-09-01.md), the [lightweight smoothness plan](archive/audits/lightweight-smoothness-plan-2026-09-01.md), the current 98-file/78-Markdown inventory, and the failed `docs/guides/update-guides.ps1 -Check` audit run that proved `cmd/gendocs` still writes to default live KB/OpenAPI paths behind a staged guide check.

**Purpose:** make every reader—CEO, product owner, normal/floor user, implementer, developer, SRE, security reviewer, auditor and legal reviewer—reach one authoritative, owned, current document for their question. This Stage reorganizes knowledge; it does not use folder movement to hide unresolved product defects or rewrite historical evidence.

**Non-negotiable rules:** plain Markdown + existing Go/PowerShell generators; no Docusaurus/MkDocs/Node documentation build/hosted docs database/new runtime service. The full `docs/` tree is not shipped to production; only the intentionally embedded Knowledge Center output/assets enter the binary/static release budget. No bulk delete, no `git add -A`, no path migration while another session is editing the same documents. Audit/UAT/incident/restore/decision/legal evidence is archived, never casually deleted.

**Dependency rule:** 48.0/48.1 may start independently once the shared worktree settles. Support/capability statements in 48.2 depend on 47.0 evidence. Security/POS/returns/WMS/audit user and normative documents must describe the real current limitation or wait for the applicable 47.x/49.x remediation—never document the intended fix as already built. Stage 47.15 closes only after 48.0, 48.2, 48.7 and the applicable 48.11 gates pass.

**Execution status (2026-09-10): implementation expanded and verified; Stage 48 is not fully accepted.** The isolated recovery capture preserves 889 hash-verified files at `fed51b4`; approval of a baseline commit/tag remains pending. The canonical drafts, 14-domain/42-FR traceability, 199-doctype/1,542-field dictionary, canonical OpenAPI projection, 49 KB topics covering all 56 registered screens, two generated manuals, strict offline lint and cached monthly external checks are built. A 24-path/five-batch migration is prepared in an isolated review checkout with retained published-path stubs; main-workspace paths and evidence are preserved. All 14 live development screenshot captures pass the repaired harness. These are technical observations, not customer, legal, product or physical-device acceptance. The [dated verification and findings](archive/audits/stage48-verification-2026-09-10.md) and [concrete migration review](archive/readme.md) record scope and remaining gates. Checked authoring/tooling items below do not imply approval of their draft policies.

## Stage 49 — Evidence-driven maximum-security program ⏳ (planned 2026-09-03; ≈40-60 sessions, continuous release gate)

**North-star, not a marketing claim:** “most secure in the world” is not an objectively provable permanent state. The product goal is the strongest practical, independently evidenced security posture for each supported deployment and industry configuration. Never claim “unhackable,” universally secure, certified or compliant. Publish the exact scope, release, configuration, controls tested, residual risks, exceptions, assessor and expiry behind every assurance statement.

**Security constitution:** secure by default; deny and fail closed; least privilege; explicit tenant/entity/location/owner scope; server-authoritative business decisions; one durable outcome per command; no shared or hidden support access; no hard-coded/default credential; no secret or sensitive payload in source, URL, client storage, ordinary log or documentation; no control silently disabled to improve speed; no security-through-obscurity; no production claim without prevention, detection, response and recovery evidence. A security control that operators cannot understand, users route around, or the team cannot patch is not complete.

**Dependency and ownership rule:** Stage 49 does not reopen or duplicate work. **47.0-47.7** remain the P0 stop-ship remediation; **47.8** owns browser/session containment; **47.11** owns bounded request/worker/side-effect safety; **47.16** owns India-first control implementation; **47.17** owns reference-journey release evidence; **48.6** owns the normative security/privacy/legal documents; existing **20.5/26.11.1** own the external penetration-test engagement; **38.2d** owns OAuth2 client credentials. Stage 49 turns those controls into one threat-led security system and adds the missing platform, SDLC, detection, recovery and continuous-assurance gates. Security, privacy, infrastructure, product, finance/control, data, SRE and qualified legal/audit owners approve their domains; an AI/developer may draft and test but cannot self-certify them.

**Lightweight security rule:** retain one Go application plus PostgreSQL and the vanilla-JS client. No mandatory WAF appliance, service mesh, SIEM cluster, secrets platform, message broker, policy engine, antivirus daemon, Node toolchain or security sidecar merely to obtain a checkbox. Prefer compile-time route contracts, shared middleware, PostgreSQL constraints/transactions, OS/reverse-proxy controls, bounded structured events and optional export adapters. A new dependency/service requires 47.18.4 evidence and an ADR. Every 49.x item records binary/static-byte, cold-start, request CPU/latency, idle/peak RSS, DB/index/WAL/log/backup growth and operator burden. Security evidence obeys approved retention/legal holds and may not recreate the audit-log space failure Stage 47 found.

**Priority rule:** 49.S0 and the applicable Stage 47 P0 items are release-blocking. 49.S1-S3 must close before an internet-facing multi-tenant Production claim. 49.S4 must close before the corresponding enterprise, regulated or contractual assurance claim. Existing module work may continue only when it does not alter the same security boundary without updating its threat model and tests.

## Stage 52 — Category-based sticker/label printing module (opened + built 2026-09-27)

User asked for a real label-printing module for a jewellery retailer: different categories need visually different labels (an earring tag looks nothing like a necklace tag), printing should start from an actual transaction (a GRN or Transfer Order) rather than manual SKU entry, whole-document or one-line-at-a-time, and the user wants full self-service control over what a label looks like via a drag-and-drop designer rather than a fixed preset. ## Stage 53 — POS rebuild: standard retail till (opened 2026-10-04 from the user's live POS report)

User, looking at the live POS screen, rejected it outright: *"this is shitty pos. who ask cust code. Make it std pos, research and make it best / it should work with name search / Bill should which loction and store / location of store sellable non saleable / it should freeze untill i reset there should reset button"*.

**What is actually wrong today** (read from `public/view-pos.js`, `engines/qz_payload.go`, `engines/inventory.go` before planning, not assumed):
- The customer field is literally labelled **"Customer Code (optional)"** placeholdered *"For loyalty points"*. A `Customer` typeahead *is* already attached (`attachLinkTypeahead`), and the server's `?q=` search already scans **every** field (so name and phone already match) — but the box shows and stores the raw code, so it reads to a cashier as "type a code you don't know". The two loyalty buttons then re-read that box and say *"Enter a customer code first."* The capability is there; the UX denies it.
- The SKU box is `Scan or Enter SKU` with an `Item` typeahead, but `addSKUToPOSCart` sends **whatever string is in the box** straight to `/api/v1/availability?sku=`. A typed product *name* produces a zero-availability phantom line, not an error — there is no barcode→SKU resolution and no result list.
- `GetAvailableToSell` already returns `qc_hold`, `damaged`, `blocked` and `hold_qty` alongside `ats`; the cart throws all of it away and prints one "Available" number, so nothing on screen distinguishes sellable from non-sellable stock.
- `Location` (`db/migrations_stage17h_location_masters.sql`) has `type` (Store/Warehouse/HO) but **no sellable concept**. Nothing stops a POS session being opened, or a sale rung up, against a warehouse or HO. The screenshot the user sent is exactly this: a till sitting on **HO**.
- Receipts print the location **code** and nothing else — no store name, no legal entity, no GSTIN, no cashier. True on both paths: the browser fallback (`printPOSReceipt`, `${location}`) and the server-built ESC-POS payload (`BuildReceiptPayload`, `b.WriteString(location + "\n")`).
- Nothing freezes. The location picker is editable mid-shift, and after `Complete Sale` the cart is silently emptied behind a confirm dialog — the next customer's scan lands on a live, indistinguishable cart with no record of the bill just closed on screen.

**Two readings were ambiguous and were put to the user before planning (answered 2026-10-04): "freeze" = BOTH (lock the store for the shift AND freeze the till on the completed bill), "sellable/non-sellable" = BOTH (a flag on the `Location` master AND splitting the cart's availability figure).**

Scope discipline per this repo's first principle: no new framework, no new dependency, no new picker pattern. Customer/product search reuses `attachCodeNamePicker`/`attachLinkTypeahead` and the existing `/api/v1/doc/{doctype}?q=` endpoint; the sellable/non-sellable split needs **no backend change at all** (the fields are already in the availability response); the `Location.sellable` flag is one additive migration in the Stage 17.9 style.

- [x] **53.1 `Location.sellable` — the master flag.** `db/migrations_stage53_1_location_sellable.sql`: `Location` gains `sellable` (Select `Yes,No`, display_order 6), additive and `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` in the Stage 17.9 style. **Scope decision — `mandatory = FALSE`, not TRUE as planned**: making it mandatory would reject a save of every pre-existing Location the next time anyone edited one, which is the "destructive rework" the first principle rules out. The gap that leaves (a Location created later with no value) is closed instead by a save-time stamp — see 53.1b. **Backfill rule changed after running it against the real dev DB, and this is the important finding of the whole Stage**: the planned "`Store` → Yes, everything else → No" rule produced **0 sellable locations out of 112**, because `migrations_stage17h_location_masters.sql` seeds every location code already in use with a *hardcoded* `type = 'Warehouse'`. Shipping that would not have been an additive change, it would have been an outage — every till in the tenant refusing every sale. The rule now has a first clause: a location with an existing `POSCart` or `POSSession` against it is marked `Yes` regardless of type, because what the business actually did is better evidence than a type nobody ever set. Re-run against the dev DB: 2 sellable (`HO`, `WH01` — the two with real POS history), 110 not. Verified by direct `psql` query before and after.
- [x] **53.1b Save-time stamp (added, not in the original plan).** `engines/master_data_validation.go` gains a `Location` case stamping `sellable` from `type` when blank (`Store` → Yes, else No), never overwriting an explicit value. Needed because 53.1 keeps the field optional: without it, a Location created after the migration would carry no value, and the 53.3 picker filter (`sellable=Yes`) would then disagree with what the server accepts — a picker hiding a location checkout would allow, or offering one it would refuse. Attached at `ValidateMasterDataRules`, the choke point every Location write already runs through.
- [x] **53.2 Enforce sellable server-side, at the choke point.** New `engines.LocationIsSellable` + `ValidatePOSSellableLocation` in `engines/location_masters.go`, returning a `*ValidationError` coded **`POSOFF-0245`** (registered in `internal/server/error_catalog_extensions.go`, HTTP 422, Blocking). Resolution order: no `Location` record → **permitted** (location is still free text on most doctypes per 17.9's own decision, so unregistered codes must keep working); explicit `Yes`/`No` → honoured; blank → derived from `type`. Called from **two** entry points: `OpenPOSSession` (engine-side, so a future third POS entry point inherits it) and `handleCheckout` (above the quote and every other side effect). Checkout is checked separately from session-open deliberately — an offline-queued sale replays through checkout *without re-opening a session*, and a Location can be flipped to `No` while a session is still open.
- [x] **53.3 POS location picker offers only sellable locations.** New generic `opts.filters` on `attachTypeahead` (`public/app.js`) — plain `field=value` pairs appended to the existing `/api/v1/doc/{doctype}` call, which already treats unknown query params as data filters. Added once at the shared control rather than as a POS-specific picker, so "Active vendors only" etc. is one line away for any screen. **Off by default — all ~45 existing pickers send the identical request they sent before.** `attachCodeNamePicker` makes two lookups of its own (resolve-on-blur, seed-the-name) and both had to be threaded with the same filter, or typing `HO` and tabbing away would have committed the exact location the filter exists to exclude. The generic Location picker on the other ~15 screens is untouched — a warehouse is still a valid transfer destination.
- [x] **53.4 Customer by name, not by code.** `Customer Code (optional)` / *"For loyalty points"* is gone. Replaced with a split display/hidden `attachCodeNamePicker(..., 'Customer')`: the cashier sees and searches the **name** (phone and code match too — the server's `?q=` scans every field via `jsonb_each_text`), `#pos-customer` still carries the code, so `checkout`, `redeem_points` and both loyalty buttons needed no change. Label **Customer (optional)**, placeholder *"Search by name or phone"*, and a live note underneath reading **"Walk-in — no customer attached"** until one is picked. Both loyalty buttons' *"Enter a customer code first."* re-worded.
- [x] **53.5 Quick-add a customer from the till.** `+ New Customer` → name + phone → `POST /api/v1/doc/Customer` → selected straight into the picker. Two fields because that is what a counter can actually get; the rest of the master is fillable later.
- [x] **53.6 Scan-or-search product entry.** `addSKUToPOSCart` no longer sends the raw box contents to `/api/v1/availability`. Resolution order: exact `Item.code` → exact `Item.barcode` → name search, all off **one** `?q=` request (the exact-match test runs on the returned rows, so the scanner path costs no extra round trip and never opens a list). Single match auto-adds; multiple matches render a keyboard-navigable result list (↑/↓/Enter/Esc) showing name, code and barcode; **no match now says so** instead of the old silent zero-availability phantom line. Both paths funnel through one `addResolvedItemToPOSCart`, so a scanned line and a searched line are identical.
- [x] **53.7 Cart shows sellable vs non-sellable availability.** New `posAvailabilityCell`: `ats` as *"N sellable"*, plus *"N not sellable (QC hold / damaged / blocked)"* only when `qc_hold + damaged + blocked + hold_qty > 0`. Frontend-only — `GetAvailableToSell` has always returned all four and the screen discarded them. A line whose qty exceeds sellable availability turns red at entry with *"Only N can be sold here"*, rather than being discovered by the server at checkout.
- [x] **53.8 Cart line controls.** `−` / `+` steppers either side of the qty box (box kept for larger numbers); `−` at qty 1 removes the line. The Item column now leads with the product **name** and shows the code underneath. Keyboard: Enter commits the scan box, arrows walk the result list.
- [x] **53.9 Terminal binding.** `applyPOSTerminalLock` called from `refreshPOSSessionStatus` (the one function that knows whether a session is open) and after the first cart line. Store box goes read-only with *"Bound to … for this session"*. **Reset Terminal** confirms, names how many cart lines will be lost, and clears them — and if a session is still open it clears the cart but **keeps the binding**, telling the cashier to close the session first: a session is a cash-accountability record, so Reset must not be a way to walk away from one.
- [x] **53.10 Post-sale freeze.** New `freezePOSTill` / `startNewPOSSale`. All three terminal outcomes funnel through one function — **paid**, **pending_approval** (orange, no receipt offered, explicit "do not hand over the goods"), **queued offline** (explicit "do not ring it up again") — so none can leave a half-live cart. The 409 `price_changed` path is deliberately *not* terminal; it re-enters checkout and freezes on whatever that returns. `New Sale (Reset)` clears cart/customer/coupon/discount/tender but **keeps the store binding** (re-picking the shop between customers would undo 53.9).
- [x] **53.11 Cash tendered and change due.** Cash-only tendered box computing **Change due** / **Short by** live, carried onto the frozen bill. Display-only and never sent to the server — treating a mistyped tender as anything more would turn it into a pricing bug. The frozen bill's change figure is computed against the server's `amount_due`, not the screen's pre-checkout total, so a server-side reprice cannot skew it.
- [x] **53.12 The bill says which store.** New `engines.ReceiptStoreHeader` / `ReceiptStore.Line()` resolving Location → name, and Location → `legal_entity` → LegalEntity → name/GSTIN/state. Wired into **both** server-side branches of `BuildReceiptPayload` (ESC-POS *and* the HTML driver fallback) and into the browser's `printPOSReceipt`. Cashier added: `storedPayload["cashier"]` is now persisted on the POSCart from the resolved identity, so the server can rebuild the full header from the cart alone. Deliberately forgiving — a missing Location, a Location with no entity, or an entity with no GSTIN each drop that line rather than failing the print, because a receipt must always print. `ReceiptStore.Line()` also de-duplicates the Stage 17.9 seed case where `name == code` (no more "HO (HO)").
- [x] **53.12b Pre-existing receipt bug found and fixed (not reported, not in the plan).** The **browser-fallback receipt printed `0.00` on every line**. Stage 47.2 made the checkout payload carry `sale_price: 0` for every server-priced line (only an unpriced assisted-mode line sends a figure), and `printPOSReceipt` was handed that same array — so `qty * sale_price` was 0 for every ordinary line and the line totals summed to nothing. It survived unnoticed because the QZ/ESC-POS path rebuilds the receipt server-side from the stored cart, so the fallback only prints in shops with no receipt printer configured. Fixed via a new `posReceiptItems()` that pairs each payload line back to its cart line and takes the resolved price (and the product name) from there.
- [x] **53.13 Tests.** New `engines/pos_sellable_location_stage53_test.go` — 20 subtests across four functions: `LocationIsSellable`'s full resolution order (including the two that would be easiest to get backwards: the **unregistered-code-still-sells** case and the **blank-on-a-Warehouse** case), the `POSOFF-0245` coded refusal, `OpenPOSSession` refusing a non-sellable location **and leaving no POSSession row behind**, `ReceiptStoreHeader`'s full/no-entity/name-equals-code/unregistered cases, and the 53.1b stamp. All pass. `node --check` clean on both JS files. `go build ./...`, `go vet ./engines/`, `gofmt` clean. Existing `engines/qz_receipt_invoice_test.go` still green after the header change.
- [x] **53.14 Guide docs, walked not summarised.** `USER_GUIDE.md` §4 rewritten end-to-end against the real new UI: prerequisites box now leads with **Sellable = Yes** (was "Type = Store", which is no longer what gates it), §4.0 covers the store lock and why a shop might be missing from the list, §4.1 walks scan-vs-search, the sellable/non-sellable figure, name/phone customer search, quick-add and cash tendered, **new §4.1a** explains the freeze and all three frozen outcomes, §4.3 rewritten around the Print Receipt button and what the header now carries, **new §4.4** (price-changed confirm) and **new §4.5** (Reset Terminal, including the session-still-open case). §4.2/§4.3 physically reordered into sequence (numbers and all cross-references unchanged). 8 new "How do I…?" rows. §13's worked example Steps 7-8 rewritten (they still described the old flow). `ADMIN_GUIDE.md` gains **§B.3.0.4** (what `sellable` gates in all three places, the full backfill rule *including the 17.9 all-Warehouse trap*, the unregistered-code pass-through, the blank-is-stamped behaviour, and an explicit "check this after the migration, do not assume it" warning) and **§B.3.0.5** (what the receipt header is built from, and that filling in LegalEntity is what makes it tax-compliant). `go run ./cmd/doclint -root .` — 322 files, 4 findings, **none in the files this Stage touched**.
- [x] **53.17 A real Reset button, separate from Refresh (user follow-up, 2026-10-04).** User, on seeing 53.9/53.10: *"There should be button of reset. instead of refresh. Refresh will have cahe and have all info but reset button will reset all."* The header's one button was labelled **Sync**, titled *"Refresh local data store"*, and re-fetched labels + registered doctypes only — every cache survived it, which is correct for "a label changed" and useless for "this screen is wrong". **Built as two buttons, not one stronger one**: `sync-btn` relabelled **Refresh** (behaviour unchanged, title/confirm reworded to say what it keeps and to point at Reset), and a new `reset-btn` → `resetClientState()`. Reset clears, in order: every `erp_swr_*` entry in sessionStorage (the stale-while-revalidate cache behind every list/metadata read — collected into an array *before* deleting, since removing while iterating by index reindexes and silently skips every other key), `erp_nav_state`, the in-memory `state` caches, the POS till via the new silent `clearPOSTillState()` (split out of `resetPOSTerminal` so the two resets cannot drift), then re-fetches labels/doctypes/permissions and re-renders.
- [x] **53.17a Found while building 53.17, and the reason Reset would otherwise have been a lie: the lazy view modules had no cache story at all.** `loadViewModule` did `import('view-pos.js')` with **no version parameter** — an ordinary HTTP GET, so (a) after a deploy a browser keeps running the previous release's screen code while the shell updates, and (b) Reset would have cleared every app-level cache and then re-imported the *same stale module* from the HTTP cache, which is exactly the "refresh keeps the cache" complaint the item exists to fix. Fixed with two additions to the URL, both reusing the existing param-composition rather than a second mechanism: a `VIEW_MODULE_VERSION` constant (**must be kept in step with `index.html`'s `app.js?v=N` on every release** — documented in ADMIN_GUIDE §B.3.0.6's deploy note) and a `reset=<timestamp>` bust set by Reset, which also re-runs each module's top-level state (frozen till, locked store) back to initial values. BLD-041's existing `retry=` behaviour is untouched. All three URL forms verified serving `200 text/javascript` against a scratch server.
- [x] **53.17b Three deliberate non-actions, each a data-safety call rather than an omission.** (1) **Reset refuses to run at all while offline POS sales are queued**, with a message naming the count — `erp_pos_offline_queue` holds *completed sales that have not reached the server*, the customer has walked out with the goods, and that is not cache. Same posture `closePOSSessionFlow` already takes for the same reason. The guard runs *before* the confirm dialog, since there is no point confirming an action that must not proceed. (2) **It does not sign the user out** — resetting a screen must not eject a cashier mid-shift. (3) **It does not reset the theme** — a personal preference is not stale data. Every storage read/write is wrapped in try/catch (private browsing, quota, disabled storage): a cache that cannot be read cannot be stale either, so none of those is a failure worth stopping for.
- [x] **53.17c Docs.** `USER_GUIDE.md` new **§12.3 "When a screen shows something that can't be right — Refresh vs Reset"** — a two-row comparison table, an explicit *"reloading the page in your browser is not the same as Reset"* (F5 re-runs against the same stored copies, so the stale data comes straight back — the trap that makes a stale screen seem incurable), the four things Reset never touches, and a pointer that at the till you usually want **New Sale (Reset)** or **Reset Terminal** instead. Plus a new "How do I…?" row. `ADMIN_GUIDE.md` new **§B.3.0.6** with the exact clear-order including the lazy-module half, the three non-actions and the `VIEW_MODULE_VERSION` deploy note. `app.js?v=` bumped 29 → 30 (and `VIEW_MODULE_VERSION` set to match). Verified live on a scratch server: both buttons render with the right labels, the served `app.js` carries `resetClientState` and the offline guard, `view-pos.js` carries `clearPOSTillState`, and the versioned/busted/retry module URLs all serve. Shell accessibility/layout invariant tests green.
- [x] **53.18 The 53.1 backfill only ever covered `tenant_default` — found while preparing the 53.15 deploy (2026-10-06).** `migrations_stage53_1_location_sellable.sql` declares the field and backfills it in `tenant_default` only, but `ValidatePOSSellableLocation` (53.2) ships in the **binary**, so it guards every provisioned tenant the moment the new build starts. On any other schema that left no `sellable` doctype_field (so an admin could not even see or correct the flag) and no value on any `Location` row, which falls through `LocationIsSellable` to its `type = 'Store'` test — and 17.9 seeded every in-use location with a hardcoded `type = 'Warehouse'`. That is 53.1's own all-Warehouse outage, guarded for one schema out of N: **every till in every non-default tenant refusing every sale**, which for prod means the `minn` tenant. New `db/migrations_stage53_18_location_sellable_all_tenants.sql` runs both halves of 53.1 across every `tenant\_%` schema, looping in the style of `migrations_stage30_2_1_grn_location.sql`; statements are dollar-quoted (`$sql$`) rather than single-quoted because the quadrupled-quote form a single-quoted `format()` needs is unreadable and was in fact written wrong the first time. `tenant_default` is included rather than excluded — both statements are idempotent, so re-covering it changes nothing and keeps the file correct standalone. **Verified on a disposable DB** reproducing the trap across two tenant schemas: a Warehouse-typed location with a `POSCart` → `Yes`, one with a `POSSession` → `Yes`, a never-sold Warehouse → `No`, a typed Store → `Yes`, an already-`Yes` row untouched, a `public_decoy` schema untouched (the `LIKE 'tenant\_%' ESCAPE` holds), and byte-identical state after two further runs. **Then on the dev DB**: `HO`/`WH01` preserved as the only two sellable, and **9 blank Locations created after 53.1 ran** (all `*-TEST` fixtures, all Warehouse, none with POS history) correctly resolved to `No` — a gap 53.1 had left open on `tenant_default` itself, since 53.1b's save-time stamp only fires on write and never touches a row nobody edits. 110 `No` + 2 `Yes` = 112. `go build`/`go vet`/`./db` tests clean. **Does not remove 53.15's review requirement**: this guarantees no location that has ever sold stops selling, but a genuinely trading shop with no POS history in the database still resolves to `No`, which remains a business answer only the user can confirm.

## Stage 56 — Railway Pro migration (opened 2026-10-04 from the user's decision)

The user purchased a **Railway annual plan (₹3,000/year)** and decided to proceed; the DigitalOcean
droplet is ₹500/month. Assessment on opening found the app is already largely PaaS-ready and the
work is smaller than a provider migration usually is: migrations are `go:embed`ed into the binary
(`db/migrate.go:19`) so Railway's pre-deploy command can apply them with no `db/` folder on the
host; an unset `HOST` binds every interface (`internal/server/routes.go:1190`), which is what
Railway needs; every secret already has an env override (`JWT_SECRET`, `CHANNEL_CREDENTIAL_KEY`,
`AUDIT_ARCHIVE_KEY` — the config-dir file fallbacks in `engines/auth.go:61` /
`engines/secret_keyring.go:123` are dev-only paths production already bypasses); job claiming uses
`FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` (`engines/jobrunner.go:261`), so Railway's overlapping rolling deploys
cannot double-run a job; and the `Dockerfile` — dormant since 2026-07-27, built by CI's
`docker-build-check` on every push so it cannot rot — already produces a distroless static image
stamped with build identity (54.6).

**Architecture decision, recorded because the alternative was the user's first instinct:** this is
**one** Railway app + **one** Railway Postgres serving **many** tenant schemas, via
`TENANT_BASE_DOMAIN` (`internal/server/tenant_host.go`, Stage 44) and `tenantctl provision`.
It is **not** one Railway app per client. One-app-per-client multiplies the metered bill, the
deploys, the migration runs, the backup checks and the version-drift risk by the client count, and
bypasses the multi-tenancy engine already built. Hosting many clients is the goal; separate
instances are not the mechanism. A contractual physical-isolation requirement from a single large
client is the one legitimate exception, and is a priced premium tier, not the default.

**Production stays on the droplet for all of 56.1-56.10.** Nothing in those items touches the live
box, so there is no window where a client is at risk. 56.7/56.8 exist because the two things that
actually decide this migration — metered cost and India latency — are measurements, not
assumptions, and both are now cheap to take since the plan is already paid for.

- [ ] **56.1 Boot on Railway with the security baseline in warn mode.** New Railway project, app
  service from this repo's `Dockerfile`, Railway Postgres service alongside. Leave `ENV` **unset**
  so `engines/security_baseline.go` logs every `[SECURITY] SB-nnn` finding without blocking the
  boot — the point of this step is to read the full finding list off a real deploy rather than
  predict it. Set `JWT_SECRET`, `CHANNEL_CREDENTIAL_KEY`, `AUDIT_ARCHIVE_KEY` from
  `openssl rand`, leave `HOST` unset, let Railway supply `PORT`. Pre-deploy command
  `./erp-server -migrate`; confirm against `-migrate-status` that the count matches the 169
  migrations `custom_erp_t1` carries locally. Done when `/api/v1/version` answers over Railway's
  generated domain and reports this commit.
- [ ] **56.2 SB-015 — encrypted database link.** `engines/security_baseline.go:283` blocks a
  production boot when `DATABASE_URL` names a non-loopback host with an `sslmode` that permits
  cleartext. On the droplet Postgres is on loopback so the rule sleeps; on Railway the database is
  a separate service, so it fires correctly. Add `sslmode=require` and confirm the negotiated
  connection with `SELECT ssl FROM pg_stat_ssl WHERE pid = pg_backend_pid();` — the setting being
  present is not evidence it was honoured. Prefer `verify-full` + `sslrootcert=` if Railway
  publishes a CA for its Postgres; record which mode was actually achieved and why.
- [ ] **56.3 SB-012 — proxy trust against Railway's edge.** `engines/security_baseline.go:251`
  blocks production when `TRUST_PROXY` is on and `TRUSTED_PROXY_CIDRS` is empty, because
  `clientIP()` (`internal/server/middleware.go:606`) would then accept any caller's own
  `X-Forwarded-For` — forging the identity that login rate limiting, lockout and the audit trail
  all record. Railway does not publish its edge proxy's address range, so this is **determined
  empirically, not from the code**: with 56.1 still in warn mode, log `r.RemoteAddr` on one real
  inbound request, then pin that range (expect a private IPv6 or CGNAT block) into
  `TRUSTED_PROXY_CIDRS`. Verify by sending a request with a forged `X-Forwarded-For` and
  confirming the resolved IP is the socket peer, not the header. Record the range and the date —
  if Railway renumbers, this silently degrades to trusting a header, so it needs a re-check item
  at cutover and a note in the runbook.
- [ ] **56.4 Volume for `media_store`.** `engines/pim_media.go:39` hardcodes `mediaStoreDir =
  "media_store"` as a relative path and the image's `WORKDIR` is `/app`, so a Railway volume
  mounted at `/app/media_store` lines up with no code change. `engines/pim_dam.go:138` writes its
  render cache to the same directory. Attach the volume, upload a product image **and a
  thumbnail-generating one**, redeploy, and confirm both survive — a container's ephemeral disk is
  wiped per deploy, so an unmounted path loses every uploaded photo on the next release and does so
  silently. Note for 56.12: a service with a volume cannot run multiple replicas on Railway, which
  caps this at vertical scaling — the same ceiling the droplet has, so no regression, but it
  removes horizontal autoscaling as a reason to be here at all.
- [ ] **56.5 Flip `ENV=production` and confirm a clean boot.** With 56.2/56.3 fixed, production
  mode must start with no blocking finding. Also set `CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` to the Railway domain
  (SB-008/011 block otherwise) and confirm SB-021 does not fire — `ENV=production` refuses to boot
  while the seed admin credential is still active (`internal/server/routes.go:40`), so a real admin
  with MFA must exist on this instance first, exactly as `deploy/README.md` Part D sequences it.
- [ ] **56.6 Prove multi-tenant hosting end to end — this is the item that makes the money.** Set
  `TENANT_BASE_DOMAIN`, point a wildcard DNS record at the Railway app, then
  `tenantctl provision` two test clients and confirm `client1.<domain>` and `client2.<domain>` each
  resolve to their own schema with no data bleed between them, both served by the single app on the
  single meter. Check `db/db.go`'s shared `dbMaxOpenConns = 50` headroom while both are live —
  go_live_decisions.md §4a.1 already flags the connection pool as a nearer ceiling than tenant
  count, and it is one pool for every tenant.
- [ ] **56.7 Measure the meter for 5 days.** The open economic question. Railway bills metered
  compute/RAM/volume/egress **on top of** the plan fee, and the plan fee is per-seat, not a hosting
  cap — so "₹3,000/year vs ₹500/month" is not yet a like-for-like comparison and must not be
  treated as one. Run 56.1-56.6 live for five days with real clicking, then read Railway's own
  usage dashboard for actual ₹/month at this workload. Costs nothing extra (the year is paid) and
  replaces an estimate with a fact. Record the number here. **Plan confirmed 2026-10-07: Railway Pro** — per-seat fee plus metered usage, so the which-plan question in this item is closed and the metered half is the only number still open.
- [ ] **56.8 Measure India latency.** Railway has no India region; nearest is Singapore, against
  the droplet's Bangalore. go_live_decisions.md:180 weighted India latency deliberately for
  GST/e-invoice/Pine Labs. Measure p50/p95 on a POS add-line and a receipt print from an Indian
  connection, both providers, same build. A cashier scanning items feels this; an admin editing a
  master does not. Verify Railway's current region list first — it changes.
- [x] **56.9 Rework backup monitoring from folder-stat to a database record.** *Built and verified
  2026-10-09 (five-item pass, item 2).*
  - **Table:** new `db/migrations_stage56_9_backup_runs.sql` creates `public.backup_runs` in the
    public schema only, since a backup is a whole-database fact. It is additive
    (`CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` + `ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS`) and applied twice locally to prove
    it is idempotent.
  - **backup.sh:** `deploy/backup.sh`'s `record_run` writes one row per run (scope
    `database`/`tenant`, outcome, file, size, duration, sha256, host). A failed run writes
    `Failed` with its exit detail. A row that cannot be written keeps the backup and posts
    `BACKUP_RECORD_FAILED`.
  - **Monitor:** `CheckBackupFreshness` reads the newest successful `database` row, so tenant
    exports never count (26.1.6). `StartBackupFreshnessMonitor` always runs. Under
    `ENV=production`, no row is an hourly alert plus boot finding **SB-026** (warn, so a fresh
    install can still deploy). Off production it stays quiet until a run is recorded.
  - **Tests:** `TestBackupFreshness` and `TestBackupStaleAlertReachesTheWebhook` cover fresh,
    stale + latest-failed, missing in dev and production, tenant export and failed run. The
    BLD-052 drill now injects a stale row.
  - **Drill:** a real `backup.sh` run on scratch DBs covered whole-DB success, tenant success,
    tenant failure and a DB without the table. Each row's sha256 matched its file.
  - **Shipping:** `deploy.ps1` now re-ships `deploy/backup.sh` (+ `chmod 755`) every deploy,
    as it already did `remote_deploy.sh`.
  - **Docs:** ADMIN_GUIDE §D, `backup_restore.md` and `incident_runbook.md` are updated.

  Original item text: The real code work
  in this Stage, and an improvement independent of hosting. `engines/alerting.go:297` resolves
  `BACKUP_DIR` (default `/opt/erp/backups`) and `CheckBackupFreshness` stats the newest
  `custom_erp_*.dump.enc` in it — and at `engines/alerting.go:310` treats a **missing directory as
  "not a machine that takes backups" and returns silently**. Correct on a dev laptop; on a PaaS it
  means backup monitoring switches itself off and reports nothing, which is the worst available
  failure mode. It also cannot be fixed by pointing `BACKUP_DIR` at a volume, because Railway does
  not share a volume between services: the app checking the folder and the job writing to it are
  different services and cannot see each other's disk. Fix: additive `backup_runs` table (new
  incremental migration), the backup job writes a row on success with size/duration/outcome, and
  `CheckBackupFreshness` reads the latest row instead of stat-ing a directory. Keep the
  `tenant_*`-exports-do-not-count rule (26.1.6). Separately, make "no backup mechanism configured"
  a **loud** finding when `ENV=production` rather than silence, on both providers.
- [ ] **56.10 Stand up the backup job itself on Railway.** A cron-scheduled service running the
  `pg_dump` → encrypt (`BACKUP_ENCRYPTION_KEY`) → retain path that `deploy/backup.sh` does today,
  writing its own volume plus the 56.9 row, with Railway's native Postgres backups enabled as a
  second independent copy rather than the only one. Then a **real restore drill** into a scratch
  database per `docs/operations/backup_restore.md` — a schedule existing is not evidence a backup
  restores, which is the lesson 2026-08-07 already taught on the droplet. Must pass before 56.11.
- [x] **56.11 Decision gate — migrate production, or keep Railway as staging/demo.** *Status: Decided 2026-10-23 (user): Railway as staging only; production stays on DigitalOcean - 134.11*
  `[needs design decision: the user's call, on 56.7 + 56.8 numbers, not on the plan fee]`. Inputs:
  measured ₹/month, measured India latency, and what is being given up —
  `deploy/remote_deploy.sh`'s staged `.prev` snapshots with commit-matched health gating and
  automatic rollback (Stage 50/BLD-005/BLD-006), `deploy/postgres_harden.sql`'s least-privilege
  `erp_app`/`erp_migrate`/`erp_backup` split, and the 49.7.3 `ufw`/port-boundary verification, none
  of which port to a PaaS as-is. If the numbers favour the droplet, Railway still earns the year as
  a **demo/trial instance** — sandbox provisioning already exists (`handleProvisionSandboxTenant`,
  Stage 38.7) and a demo that idles keeps the meter near zero. Either outcome uses what was bought;
  only one moves client data.
- [ ] **56.12 Cutover — only if 56.11 says go.** Real domain + TLS on Railway,
  `CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` repointed, database moved (small: §26.10.6 measured production as holding
  no transactional data, so this is minutes — re-measure before trusting it), re-run the 56.3
  proxy-range check, full module smoke pass, then DNS cutover with **the droplet kept warm for a
  week** as the rollback. Decommission only after that week. Per the standing release principle: no
  client data impacted, no already-set password changed.
- [ ] **56.13 Docs.** `docs/operations/go_live_decisions.md` §4 gains the revisit entry and the
  outcome (the §4 "decided 2026-08-06 — the droplet is production" call is what this Stage
  reopens); `deploy/README.md` gains or yields to a Railway runbook; `docs/ai_handover.md` §6

  when 56.6's per-client subdomains become customer-facing, which they do.

**2026-10-07 — pre-emptive fix landed for 56.1's expected first failure (`Dockerfile`, uncommitted).**
At the user's request, rather than waiting for the deploy to fail: the runtime stage's base image is
now `ARG RUNTIME_BASE=gcr.io/distroless/static-debian12:debug`, used as `FROM ${RUNTIME_BASE}`. The
`:debug` variant is the same distroless image plus a busybox `/bin/sh` and nothing else — same
`nonroot` user, same static-only contents. Reason: a PaaS pre-deploy/release hook runs its command
*through a shell*, so `./erp-server -migrate` on the shell-free image fails with
`exec: "sh": executable file not found`, which reads like a missing binary and is not one. Made an
overridable ARG rather than a hardcoded swap so the shell-free image can be pinned back with
`--build-arg RUNTIME_BASE=gcr.io/distroless/static-debian12` without editing the file.
**The ARG is declared global (before the first `FROM`) deliberately** — declared inside the builder
stage it is out of scope at the runtime `FROM`, expands to empty, and the build dies on a bare
`FROM`; that mistake was made and corrected while writing this.
Two caveats, both load-bearing:
- **Unverified by build.** Docker is not installed on this machine (`docker: command not found`), so
  this has never been built. CI's `docker-build-check` is the first thing that will exercise it, and
  Railway the first thing that will boot it. Do not record it as working until one of those passes.
- **It cannot reach Railway until it is pushed.** Railway builds from GitHub, which is at `c90e5ca`
  (2026-10-06); this change is uncommitted in the working tree. Until a commit of `Dockerfile`
  reaches `origin/main`, 56.1 will still hit the original shell failure. `Dockerfile`'s only
  uncommitted hunk is this change (54.6's build-identity ARGs are already committed in `c90e5ca`),
  so it is cleanly committable on its own — but committing/pushing is the user's call, not a routine
  dev step, per the Git Safety Protocol.
- **Retire this before 56.12** if a container path ever becomes production: a shell in the runtime
  image widens the Stage 49.S2 attack surface and is justified only while the migrate hook needs it.
  Either run migrations as a one-off job that bypasses a shell, or confirm the platform can invoke
  the hook in exec form. Today's droplet production runs the plain binary under systemd and is
  unaffected by this line.

**Carried from the opening assessment, so it is not rediscovered:** the four items that read as
alarming (56.2, 56.3, 56.4, 56.9) are ~1 to 1.5 days of work in total, not the bulk of this Stage.
Three are config-sized once the empirical value in 56.3 is known. The weight is in 56.9/56.10
(backups, done properly) and 56.12 (verification and a safe cutover) — the same shape as any
provider move: the container was never the hard part.

- [x] **57.13 Two-factor recovery code count.** *Decided by the user 2026-10-07: keep 10. No change.* *[needs design decision: user — confirm intent]*
  Reported as "10 of 10 left — there should be no limit", but "10 of 10 left" is the count of
  *unused* single-use codes, not a cap that can be hit. `engines/mfa_recovery.go:28` sets
  `RecoveryCodeCount = 10` at 50 bits of entropy each; 10 is the industry norm and Stage 49.2.3
  deliberately requires single-use hashed codes, so "unlimited" is not a property recovery codes
  can have. If the real want is *regenerating* a fresh set on demand, that already exists and may
  only need to be more discoverable. **Do not change this without confirmation — it is a security
  control.**
