## Stage 58 — Sticker Studio: a full label designer with exact-look printing (opened + built 2026-10-07; released 2026-10-09 in `f6e3961`; only 58.7 open)

Opened from the user's request to build sticker printing "with this sort of flexibility … best module ever and better than this", with a screenshot of another ERP's label designer (92 × 12 jewellery tag: size presets, DPI, stickers/row, gaps, roll/media, font family, zoom, snapping, multi-select, QR, rotated text). User decisions (2026-10-07): **printers = TSC (TSPL), Zebra (ZPL) and A4/laser sheets**; **text = exact look** (rendered at printer DPI, any font) — *"but don't steal the UI. Make it better/best UI possible and not similar UI"*; silent printing goes through the print agent, which may be our own PrintBridge (`../PrintBridge/agent/`, QZ wire protocol) rather than QZ Tray — no QZ-specific dependency added.

- [x] **58.1 Rendering engine** — new `public/sticker-engine.js`, the one renderer for studio canvas, thumbnails, browser print and thermal payloads. Draws every element on a canvas at the printer's DPI, thresholds to 1-bit, and emits a TSPL `BITMAP` (inverted bits, `SIZE`/`GAP`/`DIRECTION`/`DENSITY`/`SPEED`) or ZPL `^GFA` with standard ASCII compression (`^PW`/`^LL`/`^PON|^POI`/`~SD`/`^PR`/`^PQ`). Identical consecutive rows collapse into one image with a copy count; jobs go in 50-row batches (PrintBridge/QZ cap one WebSocket message at 32 MB). Browser path: PNGs at ≥300 dpi laid out as roll pages (CSS named `@page` per template, so one job mixes sizes) or an A4 sheet grid. Hand-written encoders, no library: **Code 128** (auto B/C subset — a 13-digit value is 123 modules vs 178 in pure B), **EAN-13**, **QR** (byte mode, v1-40, L/M/Q/H, mask penalty). Bars/modules are whole printer dots. **Verified**: Code 128 — 20 edge-case values decode exactly with ZXing; EAN-13 — 7 values incl. the ERP's own dated `0200…` codes decode with ZXing; QR — all 160 version × ECC combinations at max capacity + Unicode (₹, Devanagari) decode (159 with jsQR; v23-L, which jsQR alone rejects, decodes with ZXing); ZPL compression — 400 random/structured bitmaps round-trip through an independent spec decompressor.
- [x] **58.2 Sticker Studio** — new `public/sticker-studio.js` + `.stk-*` styles: full-screen workspace (own layout, not a copy): top bar (inline name, size chip, undo/redo, **Preview with** a real Item via typeahead, **Test print**, **Save**), icon **Insert** rail (Text, Data, Barcode, QR, Line, Box, Logo), searchable **Data fields** drawer (every label field + every Item field from `/api/v1/doc/Item/meta`; click or drag onto the label), stage with mm rulers, multi-up ghost labels, 1 mm/5 mm grid, smart guides + 0.5 mm grid snap (Alt bypasses), marquee and Shift/Ctrl multi-select, 8-handle resize, floating quick bar (rotate/duplicate/front/back/lock/delete) parked outside the label, bottom dock (zoom, fit, 1:1, Grid, Snap, **Printer view** = exact dots, align/distribute), inspector tabs **Element** (field binding, prefix/suffix, decimals, Indian digit grouping, custom text with `{field}` tokens + Insert field, font family, size mm↔pt, B/I/AA toggles, align/valign, Shrink/Wrap/Cut off, rotation 0/90/180/270, white-on-black, barcode/QR options with live **scan check**, exact X/Y/W/H, centre/full-width), **Label** (12 presets incl. 4 jewellery tail tags and multi-up, W/H, DPI, across/gaps/roll width, shift/darkness/speed/rotate-180, default font, A4-sheet layout with labels-per-page, categories/default/status/code), **Layers** (order, lock, hide); status line (cursor mm, selection, warnings: off-label, unscannable, layout size). Keyboard: arrows 0.1/1 mm, R, Ctrl+D/C/V/Z/Shift+Z/Y/A/S, Del, Esc, +/−/0, G, P. 100-step undo. New-template starter with preset cards. Templates tab is now a card gallery with live thumbnails, Edit/Duplicate and a filter. Codes made from the name and de-duplicated (verified: a second save of the same name became `-2`, not an overwrite).
- [x] **58.3 Any Item field on a label** — `engines.StickerLabel.Fields` (every scalar Item field, ≤500 chars) set in `resolveAndLogSticker`; `StickerFieldText` falls back to it, and now also understands `custom` text with `{field}` tokens and `prefix`/`suffix` (`StickerElement.Kind/Prefix/Suffix`). **Blank-value rule (both renderers)**: a field-bound element with a blank value is left off entirely, and a custom text whose *every* `{field}` is blank prints nothing (no stray "W: gm"). The server-side ZPL path (API clients of the QZ payload endpoint) skips QR/line/box/image kinds instead of misprinting them. Tests: `TestStickerItemFieldsAndFieldFallback`, `TestZPLStickerElementStage58Kinds`, Fields assertion in `TestPrintStickersBarcodeSVG`.
- [x] **58.4 Print flows rewired** — Print tab (manual SKUs and GRN/Transfer document lines) now: `POST /api/v1/stickers/print` (validation, DEVICE-0298 printer check, `sticker_print_log`) → `printStickerRun` → engine: silent TSPL/ZPL through the print agent when the Printer record has a raw language + OS Printer Name and the agent is reachable (job logged to `print_job_log`), else the browser print dialog. **Bug fixed on the way**: a TSPL (TSC) printer used to receive ZPL from `BuildStickerPayload`; the built-in default label is now drawn by the engine too, so it prints on TSC. ## Stage 72 — Item & Material Master: independent classification, sales-triggered backflush at the POS, GWP, gift cards as stored value (opened + built 2026-10-17 from the user's two PDFs)

**Why it was opened.** The user shared *Backflush vs Non-Sellable Items in Retail ERP/POS* (10 pp.) with *"Build this also for pos"* - Stage 60.4's Backflush item type only consumed components at production completion. Asked whether gift cards were in scope, they answered *"Wait. I will reshare"* and then sent the full 41-page *Enterprise Item & Material Master Module - Build Blueprint* (v1.0, 17 Oct 2026, built from the first PDF): *"Read and update checklist and build"*. Its one rule: *"Do not build Asset, Non-Asset, Gift, Backflush, Voucher and Sellable as one mutually exclusive item-type list"* - every item answers six independent questions (class, stock tracking, valuation, sellability, consumption, accounting); behaviour comes from profiles + rule tables, never from a named item.

**Decisions.** User, 2026-10-17: **short packaging stock never blocks the sale** - the default short-stock action is *Allow and report* (Block / Warn stay selectable per rule, blueprint UAT-10). Taken without asking (reversible, say if wrong): the Stage 60 **Item Type master is the blueprint's reusable profile** (section 5, "many items -> 1 profile") rather than six new profile masters, with item-level overrides - one place to configure, the existing pattern; the seven Stage 60 types keep today's behaviour except **Gift and Free With Item become Promo only** (the till could not bill a zero-priced line before this stage anyway - see 72.2); a gift's cost goes to **5170 Promotional / GWP Expense**, not COGS; gift cards are issued as their **own operation with a separate receipt**, not as a bill line (blueprint 16.1 "Separate issue receipt").

**What already existed (gap analysis, 2026-10-17).** Item Type master with barcode / batch / sticker rules and four behaviour flags (60.3/60.4); Item status = generic `documents.status`, soft delete, no Item approval rule; per-key `audit_logs` trigger (records the creator, no reason); `expected_version` optimistic concurrency (409); moving-average costing only; no negative-stock setting; no service / non-stock items; `ProductBundle` Virtual / Stocked kits exploded on OMS sales orders only; GRN -> Draft Asset per unit for Fixed Asset items (57.8); no stored value (`Voucher` is a coupon), one payment mode per bill; no void of a posted bill (returns only); offers: % / flat / BxGy / bundle price, no GWP; Location.sellable only, no item x location policy.

**How this stage is built (read before adding to it):**
- **An index, not a copy.** The PDF's own backlog rule: *"every implementation ticket should reference one capability row ... do not create another parallel master checklist"*. A row an open item already owns points there (→ 59.3); only rows nobody owns get a 73.x item. Its wave order (§9) is the build order: *"do not start a new breadth module while P0 economic correctness is still open"*.
- **Every Partial / Missing claim was re-checked against source on 2026-10-17**, because the PDF's evidence was older docs (handover, an older copy of this file, the capability catalogue). Two read-only sweeps, ~160 claims, file:line evidence in each item; the two P0 claims that open new items on their own (73.1.1, 73.1.9) were also read directly. Where the PDF is wrong: 73.0.3.
- **The 167 Built-verify rows are not listed one by one.** Their acceptance tests run through the journeys (73.J) and the existing 47.17.1 / 50.17 / 26.11.5 work; they are proven, not rebuilt.
- **Missing / benchmark-gap rows are scope decisions, not a build order** (standing rule: no new breadth without the user's go-ahead). Wave 4 lists them as input to 50.18's domain-expansion decision.
- **Numbered 73, not 72:** a concurrent session's **Stage 72** (the user's Item & Material Master blueprint - item policy dimensions, backflush rules, consumption entry, item exception queue, stored-value gift cards / vouchers; `db/migrations_stage72_*.sql`) had no section here when this stage opened; it has one now and shipped in 0845470. Where that work answers a row (gift cards, item taxonomy, a data-quality queue) this stage points at it rather than duplicating it.
- **Acceptance bar for every 73.x item is the PDF's §11 Definition of Done:** normal, partial, cancel, retry and reversal paths work; stock, tax, money and points post exactly once; rules are enforced server-side; lineage and audit exist; an authorised novice can finish the task; reports reconcile; the guides describe what shipped.

- [x] **73.1.1 A POS return appears to refund the full line price, ignoring the bill-level offer discount and redeemed points: reproduce, then fix.** `resolveOriginalSaleLinePrices` (`engines/returns.go:86-130`) refunds each line at its stored `sale_price`. The offer discount is bill-level (`pos_quote.go:389-396`, `Total = Subtotal - OfferDiscount`) and so is loyalty redemption (`pos_checkout.go:234-256`); neither is stored per line, and `returns.go` reads neither. Returning one line of a discounted or points-funded bill therefore likely over-refunds, in cash. **First** a failing test (offer bill + redeemed points, return one line, assert refund = that line's net share). **Then** persist the per-line allocation on the sale at checkout - offer share, points and their money value, tender share, a deterministic rounding remainder (PDF §6 "Partial return allocation", §6.1 step 2) - and refund from it. Foundation for 73.1.2, 73.1.3 and 73.1.6. [rows: Sale return P0, Partial return allocation P0] **Built 2026-10-17 (Batch A) - and the sale side was worse than this item says:** the offer discount never reached the GL or the tax. Every offer sale credited 4100 and debited cash at the list total and backed GST out of the list price (reproduced: 3,000 revenue / 2,730 cash / 457.62 GST on a bill that collected 2,430). Now `EvaluatePOSOffers` splits each offer across its lines (`LineDiscounts`, largest remainder by what is left of each line); the quote carries `offer_share` / `net_total` per line and backs GST out of the net; finalize posts the net (`PostSalesFinanceBookingTx` accepts a wholly free bill), caps points at the net in points not rupees, earns on the money paid, and stores the per-line `allocation` (offer, points, gift card, each money tender) on the cart (`engines/sale_allocation.go`). A return prices its units from that allocation under the sale's lock, cumulatively (`unitShare`; the net is the sum of the tender parts so a refund journal always balances), so a line returned in pieces refunds exactly what it collected; a bill sold before this rebuilds its allocation from what it recorded. **Also fixed:** `RedeemLoyaltyPointsTx` ran `FOR UPDATE` on an aggregate, so every till sale that redeemed points failed (Postgres 0A000) - now a per-customer transaction advisory lock (`lockedLoyaltyBalanceTx`). Receipt prints the posted points; POS Sale Reconciliation holds sales to the net, with tenders measured net. **Historic sales are not re-posted** (release data-safety rule): past offer sales will now read BROKEN in POS Sale Reconciliation, which is accurate - finance decides whether to journal the difference. Every step is appended to the row's history; old "Sent" rows stay as legacy. ## Stage 74 — Transaction modules master BRD: the eleven 71.7 modules specified (external PDF; opened + planned 2026-10-17, nothing built yet)

User, 2026-10-17: *"Read this and prepare the checklist for this as well"*, sharing `Enterprise_Transaction_Modules_Master_BRD.pdf` (BRD-TXN-001 v1.0, 17 Oct 2026, 46 pages, same folder as the Stage 73 PDF). Contents: §1 decision brief and the eleven gaps with P0 / P1, §2 system ownership, shared lifecycle and invariants, §3 configuration masters, §4.1-4.11 one mini-BRD per module (journey, fields, numbered FR with acceptance proof, stock / GL / tax outcome, UI brief, negative scenarios, reports, test fixture), §5 posting blueprints and refund-vs-credit-note separation, §6 print outputs, §7 roles and segregation of duties, §8 command pattern, data model and illustrative APIs, §9 screen map, §10 UAT matrix (68 module cases + E2E-01..16), §11 sixteen registers R-TX-01..16 and the reconciliation identities, §12 NFR-01..15, §13 decisions DEC-01..22, §14 waves 0-5 and pilot gates, §15 statutory sources, §16 sign-off.

**How this stage is built (read before adding to it):**
- **It is 71.7, specified.** The BRD's eleven gaps are 71.7(a)-(k) item for item (its §15.1 baseline is this file and the handover). 71.7 asked which to build and in what order; the BRD gives the order (P0 money and statutory movement first, P1 after; waves in §14) but leaves its 22 decisions open. 71.7 now points here and nothing is listed twice.
- **An index, not a copy.** Each item names the BRD section and the FR / UAT ids it must pass; the full acceptance wording stays in the PDF. Build order = its waves: the Wave 1 shared spine before any new economic command.
- **Overlaps point elsewhere.** Stage 73 owns the per-line refund allocation (73.1.1), split tender and refund to the original tender (73.1.6), transfer batch / discrepancy (73.1.7), RFQ / quote / award → PO (73.2.1-73.2.3), the GRN rejected-quantity policy (73.2.4, D05), period reopen (73.1.10), GL actor (73.1.9), report control totals (73.2.19), till cash movements (73.2.7) and the one task inbox (73.3.3). Stage 72 owns item classification (72.1), Consumption Entry (72.6) and the stored-value ledger (72.8) that store credit reuses. E-invoice / e-way credentials stay 20.30 / 20.31 / 26.2.3 / 26.2.4.
- **Every gap was re-checked against source on 2026-10-17**: two read-only sweeps, with file:line evidence in each item. The two claims that change the shared spine were read directly (`inventory.go:353-397`, `numbering.go:118-133`). The BRD itself says its gaps are "not an independently executed code audit"; 74.0.2 lists what it does not know.
- **The first principle applies to the BRD's §8 model.** Its tables and routes are "illustrative; reuse existing routes where possible". Reuse map:
  - number series → Stage 60 `GenerateSequence`
  - approvals → `approval_rules` value slabs + the existing self-approval block
  - reasons → the `ReasonCode` master
  - idempotency → `command_idempotency` / `ClaimCommand`
  - store credit → 72.8's stored-value ledger
  - registers → `ReportDefinition`
  - provider calls → `async_jobs` + `channel_credentials` + the courier adapter pattern
  - prints → Stage 63's print endpoint and templates
  - errors → `writeAPIError` (the BRD's 400 / 403 / 409 / 422)
  
  No second stock ledger, invoice ledger, approval engine or report framework.
- **Tax sign-off sits outside code.** Per the BRD, tax positions need Account Head / qualified tax professional sign-off before production (DEC-02, 03, 10, 14-16, 20). A module can be built and verified on a test client. It is not switched on for a real client until that sign-off exists. Each module ships behind a client setting, default off (NFR-15: old clients unchanged).
- **Acceptance bar = the BRD's §1.2 and its §10 execution rule.** A permissioned user can configure, create, approve, post, partly fulfil, reverse, search, print / reprint and report the transaction, and stock, custody, money, GL and compliance reconcile from the same saved ids. The evidence for each case:
  - the UI action and a readback
  - stock / GL reconciliation
  - the print
  - a denied-role test
  - a replay test

  Each module also gets its guide sections and a `docs/guides/UAT_CHECKLIST.md` section when it ships.

### 75.1 Off-box backups (P0)

Found by the review: dumps stay on the droplet (`backup_restore.md:68`), and `/opt/erp/media_store` is in no backup.

- [ ] **75.1.1** *(user)* Create a private R2 bucket with an API token scoped to it and a 30-day lifecycle rule (plus a bucket lock if offered). Put the `OFFSITE_S3_*` values in `/etc/erp/erp.env`.
- [ ] **75.1.2** *(user)* Turn on daily DigitalOcean backups for the droplet.
- [ ] **75.1.3** *(user)* Keep a copy of the production `BACKUP_ENCRYPTION_KEY` in a password manager.
- [x] **75.1.4** `deploy/backup.sh` uploads each dump with `curl --aws-sigv4` (no new tool). `backup_runs` gains `offsite_key` / `offsite_outcome` (additive). A failure posts `BACKUP_OFFSITE_FAILED`.
  **Done 2026-10-18 (module 5).** `deploy/backup.sh`: with `OFFSITE_S3_ENDPOINT` / `_BUCKET` / `_ACCESS_KEY_ID` / `_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` (optional `_REGION`, default `auto`; `_PREFIX`, default the host) each encrypted dump and its `.sha256` go to `<prefix>/database/` (a tenant export to `<prefix>/tenant/`) with `curl --aws-sigv4` and `x-amz-content-sha256: UNSIGNED-PAYLOAD`; the key pair goes to curl on stdin (`-K -`), never in `ps`. A failed upload alerts `BACKUP_OFFSITE_FAILED` and is recorded, the local backup still counts. `db/migrations_stage75_1_offsite_backup.sql` (additive, public schema): `backup_runs.offsite_key` / `offsite_outcome` + index; applied locally. Also: the script's `psql` / `pg_dump` calls take the database URL last - the Windows builds ignore every option after it (psql then exits 0 having inserted nothing), Linux accepts either order. Verified end to end on this machine against a fake S3 endpoint: dump 39.5 MB + checksum uploaded, SigV4 scope `auto/s3`, secret absent from headers; with the endpoint down the backup completed, `offsite_outcome` Failed, alert raised. *Status: Done (needs 75.1.1's bucket on production)*
- [x] **75.1.5** Nightly upload-only copy of new `media_store` files (manifest-driven), recorded as a `backup_runs` row with scope `media`.

Verified: 3 files up on the first run, 0 on the next. *Status: Done*
- [x] **75.1.6** `CheckBackupFreshness` alerts when the newest off-box success is older than 26 h. Add a test.

Dev machines and CI with neither stay quiet. Test `TestStage7516OffsiteBackupFreshness`. *Status: Done*

## Stage 76 — Short codes, store-wise transaction numbering, state dropdowns, address lines, country-correct tax IDs (opened 2026-10-17 from the user's New Vendor screenshot)

**Why it was opened.** On the New Vendor dialog: the code comes out as `Vendor/HQ/2026/000006` (no series confirmed → fallback shape with store and year), State is free text and optional, the address is one line, and GSTIN is checked against India's shape only, with no check digit and no regard to the home country. The inventory behind 76.7-76.11 found worse on the transaction side: the POS bill number is made by the browser (`POS-<store>-<epoch>`, `view-pos.js:951`), sales invoices / credit notes / JVs are 32-character `NewDocID`s, and series numbers use the maker's session store rather than the document's own store. None of those meet India's 16-character rule.

**Decisions (user, 2026-10-17):**
- **D1** Existing long master codes are re-coded to the short style, with every reference updated (user chose "Re-code everything" over keep-old).
- **D2** Transaction numbers are user-controlled **per store, per transaction** (PO, GRN, ST/TO, TI, POS bill, advance, return, MI, MR, damage, ...). A store with no series cannot transact. A new store appears in the module automatically. The final length is capped at the country's legal maximum - India **16** (CGST Rule 46(b); the IRP portal also refuses longer). No published cap was found for the other home countries, so they get a product cap of 20, shown on the screen.
- **D3** State starts blank and must be picked. It fills itself from the GSTIN when there is one, and a State that contradicts the GSTIN is refused.
- **D4** (user: "better practices are ok, but short") A master code is a prefix plus a zero-padded number, with no separator, store or year, never resetting: `V00001`. The prefix and length are asked for **in the master's own New form** the first time.
- **D5** State short code = ISO 3166-2 (`KA`; 2023 codes CG/OD/TS/UK, older ones accepted). It is filled into `state_code` on setups (Legal Entity, Location) and not shown on Vendor.
- **D6** Every address = Address Line 1 (the existing field, relabelled - no data moves) + Address Line 2 + City + State + PIN code.
- **D7** The tax ID follows the home country: India GSTIN with its check digit; 22 other countries with a certain rule; the rest get 5-20 letters/digits.

## Stage 77 — POS billing for a real store: customer capture, high-value rules by country, tenders, salesmen, hold/resume, store returns, scan without Enter, stock locations (opened 2026-10-17 from the user's POS screenshots, during Stage 76)

**Why it was opened.** Four messages from the user while Stage 76 was being built, on the POS screen. The inventory (2026-10-17) found:
- **Customer.** The quick-add asks for name + phone only. Customer has no address, anniversary, gender or PAN, and there is no default customer. The receipt prints the raw customer *code* (`qz_payload.go:542`).
- **Missing.** No high-value rules, no tender master (Cash/Card/UPI hard-coded, `view-pos.js:122`; one `payment_mode` per bill), no salesman, no hold/resume.
- **Returns.** Bill lookup is tenant-wide by exact number. A return at store B of a store-A bill just lands at B.
- **Stock.** Buckets are fixed columns plus a fixed `bin_stock.condition` CHECK. There is no stock-location master, no per-store enablement and no per-transaction from/to defaults.
- **Session close** adds item price × qty for cash bills - discounts and cash refunds are not subtracted.

**User's words (2026-10-17), the scope:**
- Customer name + number (number optional), address, DOB, DOA, gender, PAN. No number → a default customer with a default number, never printed on the customer copy; a real number is printed.
- Bill ≥ ₹50k → ask address; > ₹2 lakh → PAN mandatory - India's rule, and the equivalent for other countries.
- A tender module: which tenders each store bills with, under the user's control; reports pick them up.
- Salesman name/ID before saving - optional per configuration; different per store; always a default salesman; prompt to create one for a store; disable one who left.
- Hold bill / resume bill.
- Sales return: search the store's bills. Centralised return: SR on the original store, TO from the original store, TI at the store where the customer is, into the inward location.
- Stock locations inside a store: Main (sellable), Sold (physically gone), In-Transit (TO done), Inward (after GRN / TI), Purchase Return (warehouse only), Damage. Logic settable; a location master; enable per store; defaults applied to every new store; per transaction a default from/to; a new transaction (e.g. Damage) appears there automatically.
- Scanning without Enter, everywhere (POS, TO, TI, advance, return), typing still possible.
- POS screen: the customer messages take too much room; give the space to the products.

**Rules found (research 2026-10-17, to be held as settings with country defaults, not hard-coded):**
- India, address ≥ ₹50,000 to an unregistered buyer: CGST Rule 46(e) - name, address, delivery address, state + code.
- India, PAN for a sale of goods/services > ₹2,00,000 per transaction: Income-tax Rules 2026 Rule 159 (was 114B). A buyer with no PAN signs Form 97 (was Form 60).
- India, cash of ₹2,00,000 or more from one person per transaction/day is prohibited (s.269ST) - the cash part must be refused, the balance taken by card/UPI.
- Elsewhere, full invoice details above a simplified-invoice limit: UK £250, Germany €250, UAE AED 10,000. No rule found for the others - setting left blank.

  - **Stock locations: a master over today's buckets** - additive; enable per store, defaults for new stores, from/to per transaction, mapped onto the existing bucket columns / bin conditions so no stock data moves.

Due = Approved, not deleted, approval (latest `approval_log` "Approved"; a PO approved without an approval rule has none and counts from creation) at least N days old. Nothing received (`PurchaseOrderReceipts` empty) → `Cancelled` with `auto_cancelled`, `cancel_reason`, `cancelled_by: system`, in one UPDATE that re-checks no non-cancelled GRN names it (direct or `po_ids`), audit `PURCHASE_ORDER_AUTO_CANCELLED`. Fixtures (`DLTEST-*`, draft `PRT/HO/26-27/00011`) deleted and both settings rows removed after. One console 404 in the first run did not reproduce on two reruns of the same pages and actions.
- [x] **78.3 The rest of the day-limit set** `[needs design decision: which of these to build]` - what established ERPs do (researched 2026-10-17), each to default 0 = off: *Status: Done - all of (a)-(h) chosen by the user 2026-10-22, built as 130.10*
  - (a) **Expected delivery date + vendor reminders** - SAP: up to three reminder / urging-letter levels in days relative to the delivery date (negative = before it), defaulted from the purchasing info record; Odoo: remind the vendor X days before the receipt date. Needs an *Expected delivery* field on the PO (71.6 lists it as not held).
  - (b) **Late / early receipt check** - SAP: GR posting date checked against the PO delivery date (warning or error), plus a *latest GR date* per line. Ours: receive only within N days after the expected date, or warn on early receipt.
  - (c) **Backdated / forward-dated entry limit** - Business Central: *Allow posting from / to* on the ledger setup with per-user overrides (date formulas since 2026 wave 1). Ours: PO / GRN / transfer / return dates at most N days back (and M ahead), with a role that may exceed it.
  - (d) **GRN not billed after N days** - SAP has no built-in reminder (ME2L lists open POs with no invoice); a flag / report of receipts with no vendor invoice N days after posting.
  - (e) **Purchase requisition expiry** - a requisition not turned into a PO within N days closes.
  - (f) **Quotation validity default** - RFQ quotes already carry `valid_until`; default it to N days from receipt.
  - (g) **Transfer in-transit limit** - flag a dispatched transfer not received within N days.
  - (h) **GST statutory deadline** - input credit and debit / credit notes against a financial year close on 30 November after it (Section 16(4)); a warning when a vendor invoice / note is entered after that - a fixed date, not a day count.
  - *Status 2026-10-18:* list presented to the user; the user asked only to log it as pending - **nothing built, do not start until the user picks**. Suggested order if asked: (c) backdating limit, (d) GRN not billed, (a) expected delivery + reminders ((b) needs (a)'s delivery date).

## Stage 83 — The top of the screen: no role on the chip; a working-store switcher proposed (opened 2026-10-18 from the user's PO and POS screenshots)

User, 2026-10-18: *"No need to show superadmin in top. As it will be shown in profile. & Lets wire store selection to Top. This 2nd one think & tell me good or bad idea."*

- [x] **83.1 Role off the transaction chip.** `txnContext()` (`public/txn-screen.js`, the one chip every transaction bar uses - PO, GRN, POS, returns, transfers, journals, finance notes) now shows *user · store*; the role stays in the chip's hover text and the profile menu. Verified by rendering the chip (`admin · HO`, title "Signed in as admin (Super Admin)"); `node --check`.
- [ ] **83.2 Working-store switcher in the top bar** *(→ 85.A; decided 2026-10-18: store access per role first, then per user; All stores includes new stores)*. Today a user has exactly one store (`users.location_code`), signed into the session token; the server reads it (`Resolved-Location`) in ~19 places, store-wise document numbering (76.B) among them, and nothing records which other stores a user may work at - so an HO admin billing at Jayanagar sees *HO* on the chip while the POS store box says Jayanagar. Recommended shape: (a) a per-user list of stores they may work at (Super Admin: all; others: their own unless an admin adds more); (b) the switcher shown only to users with more than one store, a plain store name otherwise; (c) switching re-issues the session for that store on the server after checking the list - never a browser-only value, or numbering and scoping would disagree with what the screen says; (d) refused while a POS till session is open at the current store; (e) it sets the default store of new documents and the default filter of lists / reports (with *All stores* for multi-store users) - every form keeps its own visible Store field; (f) the chip and the top bar both show it. Decisions needed: who may switch, and whether lists filter by it.

Accept (Pending Order) one page. Then return. See all config in one page. It should be diff page. In Setup and Settings, config all in one looks scary. Group them and show in another sub menu ... Propose 2-3 alternatives."* - *"Manufacturing and PIMs also show as sub menu like other."* - *"Report also. It will be grouped with Sales and show sub group of Sales related in another flyout. Home will show only txn, no master data shortcut. Can't close this (RF). Inventory is diff and WMS is diff. Inv is part of ERP. Inv will have dashboard, ledger of inv and stock movement (location to location), adjustment, MRP change. All will have separate history page like we built for POS bill, PO."* - *"Update everything in checklist. It should be built and recorded, so no one should miss. We will have status of building as well."* Plan: `docs/product/navigation-simplification-plan-2026-10-18.md` (decisions D1-D14, same item IDs).

**Decisions (user, 2026-10-18, asked):** D1 Setup and Settings as a two-level menu (A of three alternatives). D2 marketplace / website orders stop at Pending until accepted or rejected, and the answer is sent to the channel. D3 Pick · Pack · Ship pages. D4 the OMS bill (own series, OMS template) goes to the customer; the ERP bill is made from it at manifest handover. D5 the OMS bill's number is the GST invoice; the ERP bill links to it and is not reported twice. D6 one Templates page under Setup, module by module. D7 Reports menu grouped by area. D8 Home shows transactions only. D9 Inventory (ERP) and WMS are separate modules. **Approved as proposed (user, 2026-10-18: "All approved which are recommended for me"):** D12 manual orders skip Pending; D13 Stock Adjustment needs a reason per line, goes through approval rules, posts ledger + GL; D14 MRP Change is item-level with an effective date and a sticker reprint offer.

User, 2026-10-18, on the deployed **Edit Item** (antique necklace; Product Family *Anitque*; More details: Sub Category, Type, Device Master Record, Device Type / Category, Polish / Plating, Metal Type, Purity, Gross / Net Weight, Stone Type / Weight, Making Charge Type / Value, Size): *"What ever is there in item master, It will be some deafult config for org. if chang required in item user will change it. While creating item it self it should ask all this. User will never revisit this. & It need to smart filled/ Auto filled with a single selction. Tax treatment will deafut taxable. Ask family mandatory in top it self. Code auto generate. Tracabity, GRN batch one company level define and Item will inherit and offcourse user can chnage required. But ask in org level. All Shelf life default take std value. Weight and ask in GRN to fill. Catrgory/Type make mandtory. Type and Famiy will create Item name it can be a+b or b+a. Allow to change once in config. It will be reversible. Purity Ask in GRN, It will hidable in GRN as well. Give in config. What ever attribute to ask in PO and GRN, Need config. Polish, Color, all will be drop down. It should ask to add in Master if not present. There will be another logic. COlor, Polish, Size etc will have one master data individually. next Categorywise there will be another mapping for color,polish and size and other attribute. This applies to all industry. Make that flexible. While Creating PO, I order for Antique Necklace- Antique will be Catgory and necklace will be type. Now red color will be attached to necklace. Once I order necklace it will show necklace related color. So, This will be a config to turn on and off. If Off all attribute will show to al. Else I ahve to map attribute to type. By dafeaut it will be all. Bring this. This should be flexible and dynamic with new master created. If on, It should where to map. Smart As well."*

Then, on the form's **Barcode and label** and **Selling and accounting** sections (every dropdown showing *— Select Option —*): *"Same goes for barcode as well. Config at org level. Account as well. Make the default for normal prod. Make it easy for user, Ask What type of product. Very easy Std option you ask and as per that change it will define the accounting drop down. Make that field mandatory to Item creation as well. The drop down should be dead easy and changeable if user do mistake."*

**Found while planning (what exists).** Code is already numbered by the server (`Item/HQ/2026/000001`). **GRN batch number** is already org-level (`inventory.grn_batch_number`, 61.6) with Item Type and Item overrides (*Item type default*). **Traceability** (`tracking_mode`) and **shelf life** have no org default - blank on every new item. **Tax Treatment** is blank on a new item. Item **Category** is free text; there is **no Type** on Item. The **Category / Product Type / Item Name** masters exist (65.3: Item Name = *Category + Product Type*, holding HSN + GST) but only the PO uses them; the Item form does not. **Product Family** on the Item is the PO's *design* (65.4: design number, vendor, design attributes, item name) - not a category; the client's family *Anitque* is being used as one. The ERP's own **Item Attribute** master exists (86.3) and feeds the Item form's Variant Options and the PO; the jewellery industry profile separately adds **free-text** Color / Polish / Size / Stone Type and fixed-list Metal Type / Purity fields to Item (`public/profiles/jewelry.json`; the 81.6 overlap). The client's Item also carries **Device Master Record / Device Type** - fields a Medical profile added before the industry changed (82: a change adds, never deletes). The GRN line has no place for weight, purity or any attribute. Nothing maps attributes to a type. **Barcode** is already org-level (`inventory.barcode_generate_at`, `inventory.barcode_per_receipt_date`, 57.7) and the eight accounting dimensions already come from the **Item Type** profile (72.1: Item > Item Type > company default = ordinary merchandise); the 13 shipped profiles are the "type of product" (Product = normal product, Packaging, Gift, Free With Item, Service, Gift Card, Consumable - Periodic, Non-Stock Expense, Non-Asset, Accessory, Backflush, Fixed Asset, Virtual Kit). But Item Type is optional on the Item, and every inheriting dropdown shows a blank *— Select Option —*, so the form reads as nine unanswered questions when a normal product needs none. **Changeable after a mistake** meets 72.12: once an item has stock history, MASTER-0407 refuses a change to its stock tracking, valuation or accounting treatment (D5).

**Decisions (user, 2026-10-18, asked).** **D1** the pick at the top of New Item is the **Item name** (*Antique Necklace*): it fills Category, Type, HSN, GST and the type's attributes; a new one is made right there from Category + Type; Product Family stays the PO's design and is not asked - *"Option1 but I may change in config saying Item name can be Type+Category or Category+Type"*. **D2** switching the name order **renames existing item names too** (and back when reversed); bills already printed keep the name they printed. **D3** values asked at the GRN (weights, purity, …) are kept on the **GRN line and its batch** - stickers and the POS read them from the batch. **D5** **free until stock moves; after that an admin-approved correction** - first answered *free until stock moves*, then (same day): *"Admin change + correction ... this is also required. Tell the impact in detail and show preview of impact and Admin approve and it will change. Warn and Change after multiple Confirmation. Are you sure one. Multiple mean no 100 times. In the std way how many time it should ask. We should give all flexibility to user. We will not build again this. May case come admin identify later after GRN."* So: until the first stock movement the kind of item and its accounting change freely; after it, a change to stock tracking / valuation / accounting treatment goes through **89.8** (impact preview → reason + one typed confirmation → admin approval → applied with its correcting journal) instead of being refused. Two confirmations, the standard: the reviewed preview with a reason, then typing the item code. **D4 taken without asking** (user: *"make that flexible"*): attributes map to a **Type** (the user's necklace example), a **Category** may be mapped too, and the more specific mapping wins (Type over Category), as Backflush rules resolve (72.3). Also taken without asking (reversible, say if wrong): org defaults live in **Configuration → Inventory** beside the existing GRN batch setting; an item inherits a default by holding *Company default*, the pattern `grn_batch_number` already uses, so changing the org default moves every inheriting item; attribute-to-type mapping works at both levels (which attributes a type has, and optionally which values); with mapping on, a type with nothing mapped still shows everything, so turning it on never empties a form.

## Stage 90 — Version numbers follow each release (opened + built 2026-10-18 from the user's Control Panel screenshot)

User, 2026-10-18: *"How come version is not changing its 0.1.0. It should be linked to the release built a mechanism for that. Like: 840909b is released. Now I want that to be mapped to our logic of 0.1.0 how it rule is set. It should update accordingly and show accordingly. I can see in control panel the mapping but it should update."*

Why it was stuck: the number came from `internal/server/VERSION` (hand-edited, `0.1.0` since Stage 14.6; Stage 54 kept it there). The Releases table reads `public.deployments`, which only `promote.ps1` wrote. A client's Version is `public.tenants.app_version`, stamped once when the client was provisioned.

| 90.1 | Numbering rule + stamping | Built, not verified live |
| 90.2 | Ledger row + client stamp at each release | Built, not verified live |
| 90.3 | `840909b` recorded as 0.1.0 | Built (runs at the next deploy) |
| 90.4 | Guides and KB | Done |
| 90.5 | Releases note says what changed | Built, not verified live |
| 90.6 | Very short text; old rows rewritten | Built, not verified live (next deploy) |

- [ ] **90.1 The rule and the stamp.** Semantic versioning from the commits since the live build: any `feat:` → MINOR (0.1.0 → 0.2.0); only fixes / docs / chores → PATCH (0.2.0 → 0.2.1); MAJOR only by hand (`deploy.ps1 -Version 1.0.0`). `engines/release_versions.go` `NextReleaseVersion`; `cmd/releasever` reads `git log <live commit>..HEAD`. `deploy.ps1` reads the live version + commit from the box's `/api/v1/version`, gets the number, and stamps `-X internal/server.releaseVersion`. `currentAppVersion()` prefers the stamp, else the VERSION file, so the sidebar, `/api/v1/version` and the Control Panel all follow. Tests: `TestNextReleaseVersion`, `TestStampedReleaseVersionWins`; `cmd/releasever` gives 0.1.1 from 840909b (docs only) and 0.2.0 from 0f2e6e1 (a feat). *Status: Built, not verified live*
- [x] **90.2 Record the release.** `erp-server -record-release` (run by `remote_deploy.sh` once the health check passes; a failure warns, the deploy stands) writes `public.deployments` (environment, version, commit, by, note "from 0.1.0 (840909b)", `passed`) and sets every unpinned client's `app_version`. A re-run adds no second row. `-version/-commit/-at` record an earlier build without touching clients. Test: `TestRecordReleaseLedgerAndClientStamp`. *Status: Done - verified live 2026-10-19: the 0.2.0 deploy printed "Release 0.2.0 (455f4f9) recorded; 2 client(s) now show it". The 0.1.0 backfill row for 840909b is still to be run (refused in-session as a remote write)*

[Waits for the user's go-ahead to push and deploy.] *Built 2026-10-22:* `deploy/remote_deploy.sh` records the backfill after each healthy deploy (`-record-release -version 0.1.0 -commit 840909b -at 2026-10-18T04:45:51Z -by backfill`); a backfill stamps no client and the same commit + version is never added twice, so later deploys are no-ops. - [x] **91.1 Reset a client to a clean slate - a standard operator action.** `tenantctl reset-data` (dry run by default; `-yes`, `-reason`, `-actor`; refuses without a backup newer than the run): removes every business record - transactions, stock, ledger, masters, company setup and settings - and keeps the logins: users with their password hashes and the roles they need to sign in, plus what the app needs to run (record definitions, permissions). Prints per-table counts before it changes anything; evidence in `tenant_lifecycle_events`. Never changes a password.
  **Built 2026-10-19 ("build all", step 3):** `tenantctl reset-data -tenant <id> [-reason -actor -yes]` → `engines/tenant_reset.go`. The plan lists every table (clear / keep / reset, rows, why) and the records removed and kept by type; `-yes` refuses unless the client is **suspended**, a backup of it from the last 24 hours is recorded (the renumbering rule, `recodeBackupStatus`), there is no legal hold, and every table is classified. One transaction; `data_reset` evidence row. Kept: users (password hashes untouched), MFA codes, roles and permissions, record definitions, chart of accounts, approval rules, loyalty tiers, stock location types, module entitlements / limits / flags, the shipped reference records (status rules, item types, TDS sections, stored-value profiles, currencies, tenders, HSN list, core attributes - rows created by `system`), and evidence (audit trail, privacy requests, e-invoice history, error log). Everything else goes, settings back to defaults and the chosen industry asked again. Done in place, not by rebuilding the schema, so the append-only triggers and per-schema functions stay. Tests: `TestTenantResetClassifiesEveryTable` (fails when a later table is not classified), `TestStage91TenantDataReset` (a provisioned client with data: refused while active and with a 3-day-old backup; then reset - only shipped records left, stock / counters / settings empty, a login's hash unchanged, permissions kept, formats shipped, evidenced once, the next PO number starts from 1). ## Stage 95 — Images for each Design and Combination ID after the PO, stored on each client's own drive (opened 2026-10-18 from the user's message)

User, 2026-10-18:

> *"We have to introduce image upload for Design and Varinat/Combination ID. Once PO doen, I will upload image. We have to build and make it read."*

Then: *"You have suggest where I shoud upload that. Once config need to build to connect for erp and the upload drive. Client to client the url will change."*

What exists: a Design is a `ProductFamily` and each Combination ID is an `Item` under it (`engines/po_design.go`). `ProductMedia` (`engines/pim_media.go`) stores images keyed by item code, on the ERP server's disk (`media_store/`, copied off-box by `backup.sh` media_sync), behind the `pim` module gate. No Go code talks to object storage yet. 75.4.1/75.4.2 planned a platform-wide bucket; this stage needs **one bucket per client**, set in config.

|---|---|---|

## Stage 98 — Print, PDF, send and export for every transaction: PDF download, the vendor's copy sent by the ERP, the right printer at each store chosen once, CSV / Excel line exports with the item matrix, attribute names you can rename (opened 2026-10-19 from the user's Send to Vendor screenshot and two messages)

User, 2026-10-19 (screenshot: the *Sent to Vendor* pop-up on a PO): *"I want to download in vendor template and Sent it to Vendor. Same for PO, GRN, TO and Sales Bill. I want a pdf download and print as well. As we have print set up. It will call diff printer for barcode and other a4 or a5 or pos bill style other style prin t automatically if all connected. ERP will be installed in 100 stores. All printer will be different. Need auto call to those printer. once erp connected. It should ask one time which printer for what txn once then nver ask. But user can change it. & I am ok if it happen automatically with out asking user in erp."* Then: *"i can download csv & excel also each txn where ever product invovled as design combination barcode qty and all other item matrixes and mrp (& add cost price in po and grn only.) & other detail as per txn po number, or grn number, vendor name & I need brand in item matrix. (Optional) User can rename atribute name like color to colour or anything."*

**What exists (found while planning, 2026-10-19).**
- The Print dialog (`printTransactionDocument`, `public/trade-docs.js`) on PO (PO / Vendor PO), GRN (GRN / Vendor Copy), Transfer (Out / In), Sales Invoice, the POS tax invoice, returns and notes: template, generating store, live preview. **Print** is the browser's print dialog (`window.print()`). **Excel** exists only for a PO (`/purchase-order/{id}/excel`, the hand-written `engines/xlsx_writer.go`, no library). No PDF download anywhere.
- **Send to Vendor** stamps `sent_to_vendor_at` and fires `PurchaseOrderIssued` at a `NotificationChannelConfig` webhook: nothing is attached and the ERP emails nobody itself. The server can already send mail (`net/smtp` with `SMTP_HOST` ..., used for account notices). The blocking pop-up in the screenshot is already a toast in the tree (92.4).
- **Silent printing** exists through QZ Tray (`public/qz-print.js`) for stickers, shipping labels and receipts. `resolveQZPrinter` (`internal/server/handlers_qz_print.go`) takes the first Active Printer whose *Default For* matches the job **across the whole company**: the Printer's Location is ignored, so 100 stores would all get the same printer. *Default For* knows Shipping Label, Invoice, Sticker, Receipt, General - not PO, GRN or Transfer. A4 / A5 documents never go through QZ.
- Every print is built by one function, `BuildPrintDocument` (`engines/print_documents.go`): each line already carries SKU, barcode, design, variant, qty, rate, MRP, tax, amount and every attribute under its Item Attribute **Label** (87). An export built on it covers every transaction at once.
- Item Attribute has a code and a **Label**; the label is what the PO add row, the prints and the 87 columns show. Industry-profile fields (the jewellery Color, Polish ...) are relabelled through Settings ▸ Customize ▸ Dynamic Labels.

**Decisions (asked 2026-10-19; answered the same day: D1 picture of the print, D2 both - the ERP emails the PDF and a PDF download is always there to send yourself, D3 per computer on the server, D5 as recommended; D4 automatic, as the user allowed; D6 and D7 as recommended):**
- **D1 How the PDF is made.** Recommended: from the pages the print preview already shows - each page drawn to an image in the browser and put into a PDF by a small hand-written writer (no library). Print, PDF, email and silent print then look the same; the PDF is a picture of the page (text not selectable, about 0.3-0.5 MB a page). Alternative: a PDF writer in Go on the server - selectable text, but a second layout engine to keep identical to the template studio, and a font to ship for the ₹ sign. A JavaScript PDF library is ruled out by the no-dependency rule.
- **D2 How Send reaches the vendor.** Recommended: the ERP emails it itself - to the vendor's email, the PDF attached, sent from the server's mail account with the store's email as Reply-To; the webhook keeps firing for anyone who uses one. With no vendor email it downloads the PDF and records the send, as now.
- **D3 Where "which printer for what" is kept.** Recommended: per computer, saved on the server - computer + store + kind of print → printer, so it survives a browser reset and can be seen centrally; a store-wide Printer record (Location + Default For) is the fallback for a new computer. Alternative: per store only - simpler, but two billing counters in one store could not use different printers.
- **D4 Ask or choose automatically.** The user allowed automatic. Planned: choose by itself when the choice is clear (A4 / A5 documents → the computer's default printer; bills → the one receipt printer; stickers → the one label printer), ask once only when two printers fit; a toast names the printer used, with **Change**.
- **D5 Prices in exports.** Recommended: PO and GRN carry cost (rate, taxable, tax, amount); a sales bill carries its own selling price (it is printed on the bill); transfers, returns and every other export carry **MRP only**.
- **D6 Brand.** Recommended: a **Brand** column in exports and in the print's item table, filled from the item; shown when any line has a brand, and a template or export can leave it out.
- **D7 Renaming attribute names.** Recommended: the **Label** on Setup ▸ Inventory ▸ Item Attribute is the one name shown everywhere (PO, GRN, prints, exports, filters); renaming never changes stored values, because the code stays.

**Order:** 98.1 exports (no device work) → 98.2 PDF → 98.3 send → 98.4 printer routing → 98.5 docs and walk-through.

## Stage 99 — Shopify: products, prices and stock out; orders, payments and refunds in; shipping sent back (opened 2026-10-19 from the user's message)

User, 2026-10-19: *"Shopify Integration. Data Custom Dasboard. CRM Moule better/best one. Store app. Add in checklist to build all this"* - recorded as one Stage each: **99** Shopify, **100** custom data dashboards, **101** CRM, **102** store app. Nothing built yet. Suggested order across the four: 100 first (no outside dependency, and 101 and 102 read its datasets) → 101 → 102; 99.1-99.7 can be built at any time against a fake Shopify in tests, only the live run (99.8) waits for credentials.

**What exists (found while recording, 2026-10-19).**
- `engines/connector_shopify.go` publishes one product with its images (GraphQL Admin API, staged uploads) and reads it back; its rate limit self-corrects from Shopify's query cost. The publish payload (`ChannelProductPayload`, `engines/connector.go`) is product-level - title, description, mapped attributes, images - with no variants, prices or stock.
- `POST /api/v1/integration/shopify/product/map` links an ERP SKU to Shopify; `POST /api/v1/integration/shopify/order` takes the orders webhook (HMAC-checked) into a Sales Order with customer name, shipping address and SKU / qty / price only - no Shopify order number, discounts, shipping charge, tax lines, payment, phone or email.
- The token and shop address are stored encrypted (`engines/channel_credentials.go`).
- Under the Stage 35.6 connector SDK, Shopify is a **legacy** connector (`engines/connector_zz_legacy_sdk.go`): pull orders, push stock and push order status are not implemented. WooCommerce has all three and is the pattern. So stock, prices, shipping / tracking, cancellations, refunds and payouts do not flow today.
- It has never run against a real Shopify store: 20.3 / 26.2.1 have waited for non-production credentials since 2026-07.

**Decisions (asked 2026-10-19; not yet answered):**
- **D1 Which side owns what.** Recommended: the ERP owns products, prices and stock; Shopify owns online orders and their payments. A price or stock edit made in Shopify admin is overwritten at the next sync, and the sync log says so.
- **D2 How the ERP connects.** Recommended: a Shopify **custom app** in each client's store, its admin token pasted once into the ERP. Alternative: a public Shopify app (one-click install for every client) - needs a Shopify Partner account, Shopify's app review and an install (OAuth) flow.
- **D3 Stock per location.** Recommended: each Shopify location mapped to one ERP store or warehouse; the quantity sent is available minus reserved minus a safety buffer (a setting), never below 0.
- **D4 How orders arrive.** Recommended: webhooks (order created / updated / cancelled, refund created) plus a pull every 15 minutes that catches any webhook Shopify failed to deliver; the Shopify order ID stops an order being imported twice.
- **D5 Which store ships.** Recommended: the store mapped to the Shopify location Shopify chose; the OMS allocation rules move it when that store has no stock.
- **D6 Shopify POS.** Recommended: out of scope - the ERP's own POS bills the stores.

**Needed from the user:** a Shopify development store (or the client's store), a custom app on it with access to products, inventory, locations, orders, fulfilments and customers, and its webhook secret.

**Order:** 99.1 connector (built against Shopify's API shape in tests, no store needed) → 99.2 setup page → 99.3 products and prices → 99.4 stock → 99.5 orders → 99.6 shipping, cancellations, refunds → 99.7 payouts → 99.8 live run on a development store → 99.9 guides.

## Stage 100 — Custom data dashboards: build your own charts and number tiles from the ERP's data, filtered by date and store (opened 2026-10-19 from the user's message)

User, 2026-10-19: *"Data Custom Dasboard"* (one of four asks; see Stage 99's opening).

**What exists (found while recording, 2026-10-19).**
- The home dashboard is a saved **DashboardLayout** (`engines/dashboard.go`, 37.11): a list of tiles, each tile one registered report shown as its table; private, or the default for a role. **DashboardDigest** emails all its tiles as one CSV on a schedule. The default is four exception reports.
- Reports come from the `ReportDefinition` / `RegisterReport` framework, already cut by the viewer's store scope and money permission.
- Fixed per-module screens: warehouse cockpit, PIM dashboard, OMS console tiles, CRM analytics (lifetime value, cohort retention). The Inventory dashboard (88.5.1) is not started.
- No charts anywhere: the front end draws none, and a tile cannot be a number, a line or a bar.

**Decisions (asked 2026-10-19; not yet answered):**
- **D1 What a widget can read.** Recommended: (a) any registered report, and (b) a **dataset** builder over a fixed list of datasets - sales lines, POS bills, stock on hand, stock movements, purchase orders, goods receipts, transfers, customers, loyalty, online orders, expenses, ledger - pick fields, filters, group by, sum / count / average. The server builds the query from that list only, with the viewer's store scope and money permission applied. Rejected: a SQL box, even for admins (another client's data, the database's safety).
- **D2 Widget types.** Recommended: number with change against the previous period, line, bar (stacked too), donut, table and pivot (rows × columns), drawn as SVG by a small hand-written helper - no chart library (first principle).
- **D3 Filters.** Recommended: dashboard-wide date (today, this week, month to date, custom), store, brand, category and channel; a widget may fix its own.
- **D4 Who builds, who sees.** Recommended: a **Build dashboards** permission; share with users, roles or stores; every viewer sees only their own stores' data, and money only if their role may, so one dashboard serves every store manager.
- **D5 How fresh.** Recommended: loaded on open and refreshed every 5 minutes while open (a setting); each widget's result kept for 60 seconds on the server so 100 stores opening the same dashboard do not each hit the database.

**Order:** 100.1 data layer → 100.2 charts and the widget editor → 100.3 dashboards, sharing, ready-made set → 100.4 guides and walk-through.

## Stage 102 — Store app: an app on the phone or tablet for store staff - today's sales, approvals, scan an item, receive, count, print a label, serve a customer (opened 2026-10-19 from the user's message)

User, 2026-10-19: *"Store app"* (one of four asks; see Stage 99's opening). Earlier, 2026-10-18 (55.5a): *"we will build a PWA for the approval"*.

User, 2026-10-22: *"Stage 101 CRM: about 35. Stage 102 store app: about 10 left. Build all"* - every open item below built in one run. D4 is decided, so the shared-phone sign-in it describes is now its own item, 102.1.4. 102.2.1 is built on its own read call because Stage 100's datasets do not exist yet; Stage 100 can take that call over as a dataset.

**What exists (found while recording, 2026-10-19).**
- The ERP is a web app laid out for a desktop or till screen: no app manifest, no service worker, nothing to install on a phone.
- The POS keeps selling offline: sales queue in the browser and sync when the line returns, with a heartbeat and a gap check (20.13; POS Offline Gaps).
- Pieces a store app would reuse: store access per user and the working store (85), the approval engine and the task inbox (73.3.3), scan-to-age lookup (61), the RF traceability screens (`public/view-rf-traceability.js`), sticker printing through QZ Tray (desktop only), and the second approval for returns, built and switched off (55.5a).

**Decisions (asked 2026-10-19; D1, D2 and D5 answered the same day - user, replying to "for store staff rather than shoppers? an installable web app with no app store and no new framework? phone billing stays out of the first version": *"We can build a pwa"* - all three as recommended. D3 and D4 not yet answered):**
- **D1 Who it is for.** **Decided: store staff** - manager, cashier, salesman, stock staff. A shopping app for the brand's customers is a different product (Shopify's own mobile store, with Stage 99, covers online buying).
- **D2 How it is built.** **Decided: an installable web app (PWA)** served by the same server at `/store/`, plain JavaScript like `public/` - installed from the browser, no app store, updated on next open; a Play Store listing later by wrapping the same app (TWA) if wanted. Rejected: a native, Flutter or React Native app (a new framework and build step; first principle).
- **D3 Offline.** Recommended: item, price and stock lookups work from the last download; counts and scans queue offline and sync later; approvals need a connection. *Until answered:* the app itself opens offline and says it is offline; lookups and approvals need a connection.
- **D4 Signing in on a shared phone.** Recommended: the manager registers the phone to the store once; each person then signs in with their own PIN, locked after a few idle minutes (49.14.3). *Until answered:* the app uses the ERP's own sign-in (password, then the two-factor code where the role needs it; the Stage 67 shift session) - right for a personal phone; the PIN is added on top once decided, with no rework.
- **D5 Billing on the phone.** **Decided: not in the first cut** - a salesman builds the basket on the phone and the till recalls it (77's hold / resume); full billing on a tablet later if asked.

**Order:** 102.1 the app shell → 102.2 manager → 102.3 stock → 102.4 selling floor → 102.5 guides and real-phone checks. **First slice (started 2026-10-19):** the parts that need no other stage - 102.1.1 the installable app, 102.1.2 camera scanning, 102.2.2 approvals and 102.3.1 scan an item. 102.2.1 waits for Stage 100's datasets, 102.3.4 for 98.4, 102.4.1 for 101.1.

- [x] **104.1 An empty report is not logged as an error.** `handleRunReport` logged REPORT-0160 on every report with no rows, although its own comment calls that a normal, non-blocking 200 answer. Keep the code / message annotation on the response; drop the log write. *Status: Done* - `internal/server/handlers_report_engine.go`; `TestEmptyReportIsNotLoggedAsError` (200 + REPORT-0160 note, no row for its correlation id).
- [x] **104.2 Errors (24h) and the sustained-error-rate alert count faults only.** A row whose message starts with a catalog code the catalog answers with 2xx / 4xx (a request the user can correct) is a rejection, not a fault; worker errors, panics and 5xx answers still count. Severity cannot tell them apart (163 High / Critical codes are 4xx rejections such as GOODSR-0096). `internal/server` hands the code list to `engines` (which cannot import the catalog); the Control Panel count + its "last" time and `checkErrorRate` filter on it. Rows stay in the log (Activity Log → System Errors, correlation-id lookup). Applies to old rows too, so prod's 36 read 0 after the release. *Status: Done* - `engines.ClientErrorCodes` / `systemFaultSQL` (`engines/logs.go`), set lazily from the catalog in `internal/server/apierror.go` (an extension row added by another init is included); `engines/platform_control_panel.go`, `engines/alerting.go`. ## Stage 109 — One click to release, one click to deploy, the server cleans itself; SSH bots blocked (opened 2026-10-19 from the user's message)

User, 2026-10-19: *"I want auto mechanism to do this ... What you are doing for push to github. I want a mechanism what are you checking a script or bot to build for me to do all that ... It should learn parallely with you doing in future. Once you say all loophole close, I will run that ... Next for deployment in server and Clean up of server ... Three action three click. 3rd one if can be done without me also fine. Like a scheduler in erp or server."* Then, on the SSH note: *"How to fix this"*.

**Decisions (made here, from the user's "tell the suitable way"):** D1 the release and deploy are PowerShell scripts in the repo started by double-click `.cmd` files at the root, like `Open-ERP.cmd` - no new tools or dependencies. D2 the cleanup runs on the server as a root cron job, not inside the ERP: it needs root, must work when the ERP is down, and keeps the ERP light. D3 the deploy click shows every pending migration that changes client data and waits for the user to type YES - it replaces Claude's questions before a deploy. D4 work that must not ship is listed in `deploy/release-hold.txt` (git-ignored); the release leaves those paths out. D5 the gates live in one script plus `deploy/RELEASE_GATES.md`; a session that meets a release step the script missed adds it there in the same session (CLAUDE.md rule). D6 SSH bots: sshguard (C, ~2 MB RAM), not fail2ban (Python, ~30 MB) and not ufw `limit` (a deploy opens ~9 SSH connections in under a minute and would lock itself out).

Decisions (user, 2026-10-20/21, chat): **D1** open any client from app.wholeops.in with your own login - one password, one authenticator. Not one key copied into every client: each client stores its key as plain text (`engines/mfa.go:131`), so one leaked client would expose all. **D2** the support user each client gets is hidden from that client. **D3** an opened session lasts as long as a normal login. **D4** you are the only Super Admin; a client's top account is **Admin** - everything in their business except Setup & configuration, Users & roles, Integrations & keys, Audit & privacy and the Data Console (revised by 125.6: Admin gets all of it; only developer tools stay Super Admin). **D5** Admin keeps the authenticator. **D6** live clients' Super Admin accounts become Admin.

- [x] **125.1 Admin role** (user, 2026-10-21: *"Client only will have admin access. I will be only Super admin."*). New built-in role `Admin`. `IsSuperAdmin` stays strict (Super Admin / legacy HR/Admin), so the 101 admin-only routes (`LevelAdmin`) and any future check fail closed for Admin; a new `HasFullAccess` (Super Admin or Admin) replaces it at the business-power checks (built-in full record access, every store, approvals, GRN steps, period close, exports) - each of the 72 call sites classified. `RequiresMFA` covers Admin. The menu hides the vendor-only screens from Admin. Built as planned: about 45 business checks moved to `HasFullAccess`; `checkPermission` uses `FullAccessAllows` (Admin reads `AdminReadOnlyDoctypes` - status rules, webhooks, notification channels, robotics credentials, password-reset history - but cannot change them); menu admin-only items follow `is_super_admin`; `cmd/reset_mfa -all-admins` covers Super Admin and Admin. Verified: `TestStage125AdminRole`, `TestStage125AdminGates`, full suite; live, an Admin sees no Settings menu, gets 403 on `/admin/users`, `/admin/settings` and a StatusTransitionRule create, 200 on purchase orders. *Status: Done*

Normal login refuses the support user; it is left out of the client's Users list and user pickers. Every opening goes to the client's audit log and evidence trail with the operator's name. Built in `engines/platform_support.go`, `internal/server/handlers_platform_support.go`, `public/view-handoff.js`, `db/migrations_stage125_2_platform_support_user.sql`. Username `wholeops-support`; its password is not a bcrypt hash, so no login can match it (no login-query change needed); hidden through `NotSupportUserSQL`, which tolerates a schema the migration has not reached.
